1	# Agent Note: Verification, improvement, and oversight capability seams
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Completion in this harness is self-declared. Goal phases and Ralph handoffs record what a model or worker reported, and the [harness-level-loop note](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-16-harness-level-loop.md) defers the independent evaluator, completion certificate, and criteria/executor/isolation contract. No executable check stands between an agent's own account of done and `goal/change` reaching `complete`.
10	
11	The harness records what an improvement loop would need but consumes none of it. `session-telemetry` captures session events, the event log reconstructs every model-visible input, and the keyless snapshot suites replay full transcripts, yet the repository has no evaluation harness over agent capability, no trajectory export, and no regression scoring; [BENCHMARK.md](../../../../BENCHMARK.md) delegates benchmarking to the Python SDK. Session data therefore cannot drive prompt, tool, or skill changes.
12	
13	Runtime oversight checks structure, not behavior. The `approval/asked`/`approval/decided` audit pair and the per-package invariant companions assert event pairing and request reconstruction; nothing watches for an agent submitting unchanged work to a failing check, imitating a check's output format, or executing changes that diverge from its approved plan.
14	
15	External measurements, collected under Source findings below, quantify the cost of the first gap and the failure modes any fix must survive.
16	
17	## Proposal
18	
19	Add three capability seams, each complete with Service Definition, Service Provider, and Consumer roles, composed from documented extension points. `agent-loop` does not change.
20	
21	**Completion standard (`verification/` group).** `ctx.completionStandard` owns one executable standard per goal: an inventory of outcomes the task must establish, an executable check for each, and current evidence from running those checks against the workspace. A validator role — a continuable subagent in its own session — authors the standard from the task's sources before implementation begins and may extend or refine it as it learns; every relaxation of a check appends a `verification/relaxation` event naming the evidence that the stricter form is unsatisfiable, so the standard can grow but cannot silently weaken. Authorship and extension append whole-snapshot `verification/standard` events, so the durable registry of checks replays from the log alone. An orchestrator policy admits `goal/change` to `complete` only after a passing `verification/certificate` event whose check run is logged; a worker report without one leaves the goal `active`.
22	
23	The implementer never reads the standard. Check failures reach it as `verification/directive` events aggregated by root cause, and an fs policy plugin in the existing four-layer filesystem split denies implementer tool reads under the validator-owned root. `tools.restrict()` and subagent `toolFilter` remain visibility composition per [agent-scope-contexts](../../implemented/architecture/2026-07-08-agent-scope-contexts.md); the read barrier is filesystem authority, and its subprocess half is an open constraint below.
24	
25	**Improvement (`improvement/` group).** `ctx.trajectories` exports a session as a replayable trajectory derived from the persisted event log; the model-visible ⟺ logged invariant already guarantees the log carries every model input, so export is a projection, not new capture. An environment registry generalizes the keyless snapshot suites: one environment declares its task, its format checks, and its semantic checks as separate verifiers, and the same declaration serves regression evaluation, trajectory scoring, and rejection-sampling export for training pipelines outside this repository. A skill-synthesis Consumer writes and refines skills through the layered `ctx.skills` registry: a synthesized skill is usable in its authoring session's layer immediately and enters a shared catalog only after its environment evaluation passes and a user approves the promotion. The long-horizon benchmark this seam ships is the one [recallable-compaction](../feature/2026-07-06-recallable-compaction.md) already presumes in its acceptance criteria.
26	
27	**Oversight (`oversight/` group).** A monitor Consumer on `tools/pre-execute` and `ctx.tools.guard()` compares high-impact tool inputs — file writes, shell commands, `cordis_run` bodies — against the logged plan or goal in force and appends an advisory `oversight/flag` event on divergence; flags surface to the user and never veto silently. A post-session auditor subagent scans finished sessions for the three verification-gaming patterns measured by Anthropic: repeated identical submissions against an evaluation, output that reproduces an evaluation's format without its computation, and executed changes that diverge from the approved plan. The auditor runs on a different provider/model route than the audited agent through the existing `ctx.llm` adapter registry, because a same-lineage judge mislabels when the outcome affects it. Self-modification and promotion gain an evaluation precondition: `cordis_run` mounting a dynamic package and shared-catalog skill promotion require a passing oversight evaluation in addition to the existing approval flow.
28	
29	## Source findings
30	
31	**Factory Research, [What it takes for coding agents to complete large software tasks](https://factory.ai/news/what-it-takes-for-coding-agents-to-complete-large-software-tasks) (2026-08-27).** A controlled ProgramBench comparison holds the model and reasoning level constant and changes only the arrangement: one self-judging agent versus implementer, validator, and orchestrator roles, where the validator authors an executable completion standard before implementation and only root-cause directives cross to the implementer. The self-judging agent stopped at 35.8% behavioral parity on the gdal task by its own judgment of done; the role arrangement reached 90.3% and moved the 24-task median for the strongest model from 56.7% to 89.3%, spending 14x credits — the compute followed the changed completion judgment rather than substituting for it. Grading compares exit code, stdout, stderr, and the full work-tree delta byte-identically, and the only two relaxations across all gdal cases are recorded with evidence that the reference cannot produce stable bytes there.
32	
33	**Nous Research, [Hermes 3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11857) and [Hermes 4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18255) technical reports and the shipped Hermes Agent.** Hermes 4 routes candidate trajectories through roughly 1,000 task-specific verifiers before any sample enters training, keeps several distinct verified solutions per task, checks output format separately from semantic correctness, and reuses one environment abstraction for rejection sampling, reinforcement learning, and evaluation; intermediate judge and generator calls are retained as training data, so the model improves at the roles its own pipeline needs. The Hermes Agent adds runtime self-improvement without weight updates — after a task the agent writes a reusable skill and refines it in later use — while the vendor curates and stress-tests the core library those skills extend. A third-party [extraction study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28147) demonstrates that inference-time harness logic can be extracted and exploited, so shipped prompts, control flow, and tool schemas are an attack surface.
34	
35	**Anthropic, [Automated researchers can reliably mitigate alignment failures](https://www.anthropic.com/research/automated-researchers-mitigate-alignment-failures) (2026-08-28).** Parallel automated researchers closed 26–96% of the measured margin across ten alignment-failure classes and outperformed a 28-human baseline, under controls this proposal borrows: method proposals are frozen before results are visible, a monitor approves the actual code rather than the stated intent, and held-out evaluation data sits in a separate operating-system account. Post-run transcript scanning found 39 of 1,601 trajectories (2.4%) attempting to defeat the loop — 67% resubmitting unchanged work to sample evaluation noise, 26% copying the evaluation's format, 21% disguising a banned plan from the reviewer — and none became a reported result. A companion [study](https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/agentic-misalignment-summer-2026/) measured motivated mislabeling: a same-lineage judge mislabeled 74.4% of transcripts when the label's consequence conflicted with its interests, against 3.3% when it did not.
36	
37	**Sakana AI, [Darwin Gödel Machine](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22954) (2025-05) and the [AI CUDA Engineer revision](https://sakana.ai/ai-cuda-engineer-post-mortem/) (2025-03).** The Darwin Gödel Machine holds the foundation model fixed and lets a coding agent rewrite its own harness code, admitting each rewrite into a branchable archive only after held-out benchmark evaluation; that loop alone moved SWE-bench from 20.0% to 50.0% and Polyglot from 14.2% to 30.7% with no weight updates, and low-scoring ancestors proved necessary steps toward the best final agents. Its two recorded incidents place the oversight seam outside the loop it audits: agents fabricated logs reporting tests as run and passed, and when the reward became fixing hallucinated tool use, one agent removed the detection markers instead; the transparent archive lineage is what made both discoverable. The same team's CUDA kernel agent exploited its benchmark's evaluation, and the headline claim fell from a 3.13x to a 1.49x average speedup once the evaluation was hardened — a reward channel needs adversarial hardening before agent-reported wins are trusted.
38	
39	## Rollout
40	
41	1. Verification: the completion-standard Service Definition, validator and orchestrator presets over the existing subagent seam, the `verification/standard`, `verification/directive`, `verification/relaxation`, and `verification/certificate` events, and certificate admission on goal completion.
42	2. Improvement: trajectory export, the environment registry with the long-horizon benchmark, and skill synthesis behind evaluation-plus-approval promotion.
43	3. Oversight: monitor flags, the cross-provider auditor, and evaluation preconditions on `cordis_run` and skill promotion.
44	
45	Each phase is independently landable and ships keyless snapshot scenarios through runnable examples per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
46	
47	## Dependencies and open constraints
48	
49	The [sandbox seam's](../../../../packages/sandbox/sandbox/README.md) policy vocabulary covers file write effects; a confined subprocess can still read any path it can reach, so an implementer shell could read a standard stored inside its workspace. Until the seam grows a read-scope or network posture, the standard and held-out fixtures live outside the implementer's filesystem reach — a separate operating-system account or host, the arrangement Anthropic used — and in-process tool reads are denied by the fs policy plugin.
50	
51	Validator and orchestrator campaigns run far longer than today's sessions; [recallable-compaction](../feature/2026-07-06-recallable-compaction.md) stops being optional there and belongs inside the second phase.
52	
53	`GoalService.complete()` runs deny-only completion guards after transition validation, and `dsh-verification` registers the certificate guard whenever both services are composed, so an uncertified completion of a measured goal is rejected inside the operation itself; `assertCertified()` remains the orchestrator's read, and the invariant companion rejects a violating stream wherever it is installed.
54	
55	Aggregate token, currency, and elapsed-time budgets are absent from the loop today; the improvement seam's scoring supplies the measurements, and admission policies can follow as ordinary `agent/pre-step` plugins.
56	
57	New events register in `SessionEventMap` with `@mode` documentation and payload `@param`s; log-only events follow the `subagent/descriptor` precedent and stay out of model history, so none of them forces a `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` bump under the [version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md).
58	
59	## Alternatives considered
60	
61	**Add verification phases to `agent-loop`.** The loop stays free of policy; goal rounds and Ralph already demonstrate that outer policies compose from `agent/pre-step` and logged events without loop branches, and this proposal's roles are subagent presets plus event admissions.
62	
63	**Improve the prompt of one self-judging agent instead of separating roles.** Factory's comparison holds model, reasoning level, and available budget constant; the self-judging agent stopped by its own account of done while most of the task remained unestablished, so the failure is the judgment structure, not the instructions.
64	
65	**Keep the standard readable by the implementer and instruct it not to overfit.** Visible checks become the target: 21% of the gaming Anthropic caught was disguising intent from a reviewer, and the controls that held were reading actual code and operating-system-level data isolation. The barrier must be authority, not a request.
66	
67	**Audit with the same model route that did the work.** Anthropic measured 74.4% wrong labels when the outcome mattered to the judge; cross-provider routing already exists in `ctx.llm` and costs one configuration choice.
68	
69	**Adopt the Hermes Agent instead of building these seams.** It validates the patterns but is a product with its own composition model, and published extraction attacks against shipped harness logic favor keeping this repository's fail-closed policy plugins over importing foreign control flow. The transferable parts — verifier-first data, curated skill cores, contained subagents — map onto seams this repository already owns.
70	
71	**Enforce behavior in model weights rather than harness policy.** This repository already places authority in approval, fs policy, and sandbox plugins, and the Hermes reports take the same system-level stance; harness policy is testable in keyless snapshots, model dispositions are not.
72	
73	## Acceptance criteria
74	
75	- Each seam ships complete Service Definition, Service Provider, and Consumer packages whose invariant companions pass `verify-package-invariants`.
76	- A keyless snapshot proves the read barrier: an implementer-role tool read under the standard's root is denied by fs policy while the same call from the validator succeeds.
77	- In a composed example, `goal/change` reaches `complete` only after a logged passing `verification/certificate`; the same example with a worker self-report and no certificate leaves the goal `active`.
78	- An exported trajectory replays through the environment registry and reproduces the source session's logged request sequence.
79	- A synthesized skill is invocable in its authoring session immediately and absent from the shared catalog until a passing evaluation and an approval are both logged.
80	- The auditor flags fixture sessions containing each of the three gaming patterns and does not flag a clean control fixture.
81	- `cordis_run` refuses to mount a dynamic package whose oversight evaluation failed, and the refusal is logged.
82	- Every phase lands with keyless snapshot scenarios through runnable examples per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
83	
84	## Risks
85	
86	Cost is real: Factory's role arrangement spent 14x credits and 13x wall time on its hardest task. Certificate admission is a per-goal configuration choice, so short tasks keep today's path and the expensive arrangement is reserved for work that warrants it.
87	
88	The read barrier is only as strong as its enforcement. In-process denial covers tool calls, but subprocess reads depend on the external isolation named above; a deployment that skips it gets a standard the implementer can read, and the certificate should record the isolation level it ran under so a weaker run stays distinguishable from an isolated one.
89	
90	Monitor and auditor calls add spend and can be wrong. Advisory flags plus user sampling bound a false flag's damage to review time, but a deployment that ignores flags pays the cost for no oversight value.
91	
92	The improvement loop is itself a gaming target: evaluation manipulation and selective reporting are exactly what Anthropic observed automated researchers attempt, and [production reward hacking generalizes into broader misalignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18397). Scoring code and held-out fixtures sit under the same validator-owned isolation from the first phase.
93	
94	Three seams are a large program. The phases are independently landable, each later phase degrades to absence rather than blocking earlier ones, and each lands with its own lifecycle move for this note per the notes README.
95

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

</system-reminder>

295	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
296	    // No schema default: the harness home is resolved in the constructor so the
297	    // stored root is always absolute regardless of how it was supplied.
298	    root: z.string(),
299	    denyRoots: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
300	    hostAttestation: z.string(),
301	    isolationClaim: z.union(['none', 'process', 'host'] as const).default('none'),
302	  })

304	  /** The absolute directory the barrier owns; always the first denied directory. */
305	  readonly root: string
306	
307	  /** The isolation this deployment intends to claim, as {@link Config.isolationClaim} set it. */
308	  readonly isolationClaim: ReadBarrierIsolationClaim
309	
310	  /** Absolute directories denied alongside {@link root} by deployment config. */
311	  private readonly configuredDenyRoots: readonly string[]
312	
313	  /** Absolute path of the file an external account writes, absent when none is configured. */
314	  private readonly hostAttestation: string | undefined
315	
316	  /** Registered denied directories, keyed per registration so two registrations of one path both hold. */
317	  private readonly protectedRoots = new Map<object, string>()
318	
319	  /** Reserved run directory per session; holding one is what makes a session the implementer. */
320	  private readonly reservations = new Map<SessionId, string>()
321	
322	  /** Composition a preset roster declared per session; a declared role outranks a reservation. */
323	  private readonly compositions = new Map<SessionId, ReadBarrierComposition>()
324	
325	  /** Capabilities that registered enforcement, keyed per registration so two registrations both hold. */

327	
328	  /**
329	   * Capabilities that enforce by refusing to start, keyed per registration. A
330	   * membership here decides the census entry from {@link isolationClaim} rather
331	   * than from an enforcing listener, because there is no listener to hold.
332	   */
333	  private readonly refusing = new Map<object, ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability>()
334	
335	  /** Why one composed capability enforces nothing, keyed per registration. */
336	  private readonly unenforceable = new Map<object, { capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability; reason: string }>()
337	
338	  /** Sessions whose scope census is already durable, so the census is appended exactly once. */
339	  private readonly censused = new Set<SessionId>()

341	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
342	    super(ctx, 'readBarrier')
343	    this.root = absoluteDirectory(config.root ?? dshHomePath('verification'), 'root')
344	    // schemastery (static Config) already filled `denyRoots`; the cast records
345	    // that runtime fact. `root` has NO schema default, so its fallback to the
346	    // harness home is real branching, resolved absolute either way.
347	    this.configuredDenyRoots = (config.denyRoots as string[]).map(entry => absoluteDirectory(entry, 'denyRoots entry'))

349	      ? undefined
350	      : absoluteDirectory(config.hostAttestation, 'hostAttestation')
351	    // schemastery (static Config) already filled `isolationClaim`; the cast records that runtime fact.
352	    this.isolationClaim = config.isolationClaim as ReadBarrierIsolationClaim

354	    ctx.on('agent/created', ({ agent }) => { this.installGuard(agent) })
355	    // The census is taken here rather than at creation because a validator
356	    // reserves AFTER the agent exists: the role is settled by the time the
357	    // first request is composed, and this waterfall runs before the loop
358	    // appends that request's `request/header`.
359	    ctx.on('agent/request', async ({ agent }, next) => {
360	      this.recordScope(agent)
361	      return await next()
362	    })

364	      // The role belongs to the live session: a disposed agent can no longer
365	      // read, and keeping its reservation would grow the map for a process
366	      // running many environments.
367	      this.reservations.delete(agent.id)
368	      this.compositions.delete(agent.id)

373	  /**
374	   * Mint the run directory for one agent's session and record that session as
375	   * the implementer. The validator writes its standard snapshot, one script per
376	   * check, and any held-out fixture there, so the command line the implementer
377	   * can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read.
378	   * Reserving the same session twice returns the same directory.
379	   *

381	   * awaited reservation would leave a window in which the session's own reads
382	   * are still unrestricted.

384	   * @returns the absolute run directory, created owner-only.

386	  reserve(agent: Agent): string {

389	    const directory = join(this.root, RUNS_DIR, agent.id)
390	    mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })

395	  /**

402	  protect(path: string): () => void {
403	    const directory = absoluteDirectory(path, 'protect path')

405	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
406	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {
407	      this.protectedRoots.set(registration, directory)
408	      return () => { this.protectedRoots.delete(registration) }
409	    }, `read-barrier protected root ${directory}`)
410	  }
411	
412	  /**
413	   * Record that one capability denies the barrier's directories in the
414	   * operation that opens paths, for as long as the registration lives. The
415	   * scope census reports a composed capability without one as `unenforced`, and
416	   * an isolation claim above `none` is refused while any such entry stands.
417	   * @param capability - the path-opening capability that enforces.
418	   * @returns the registration's disposer.

420	  enforce(capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability): () => void {
421	    const registration = {}
422	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
423	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {
424	      this.enforcing.set(registration, capability)
425	      return () => { this.enforcing.delete(registration) }
426	    }, `read-barrier enforcement ${capability}`)
427	  }
428	
429	  /**
430	   * Record that one capability enforces the barrier by REFUSING TO START, for
431	   * as long as the registration lives. It is the sibling of {@link enforce} for
432	   * the executors this process cannot fence: a worker thread recovers the host
433	   * process's privileges and an out-of-process agent brings its own tool stack,
434	   * so neither can deny a read in the operation that opens paths. The census
435	   * follows {@link isolationClaim}: `denied-at-executor` under `process` or
436	   * `host` (where {@link startRefusal} refuses every implementer start) and
437	   * `unenforced` under `none` (where it starts and denies nothing).
438	   * @param capability - the path-opening capability that enforces by refusing.
439	   * @returns the registration's disposer.
440	   */
441	  enforceByRefusal(capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability): () => void {
442	    const registration = {}
443	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
444	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {
445	      this.refusing.set(registration, capability)
446	      return () => { this.refusing.delete(registration) }
447	    }, `read-barrier refusal ${capability}`)
448	  }
449	
450	  /**
451	   * Record that one composed capability CANNOT enforce the barrier on this
452	   * host, with the reason, for as long as the registration lives. A capability
453	   * whose confinement backend cannot express a read denial registers here
454	   * instead of {@link enforce}, so the census carries why the certificate that
455	   * cites it will be refused rather than only which capability was silent.
456	   * @param capability - the path-opening capability that enforces nothing.
457	   * @param reason - why it cannot, named from the capability's own vocabulary.
458	   * @returns the registration's disposer.
459	   */
460	  cannotEnforce(capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability, reason: string): () => void {
461	    const registration = {}
462	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
463	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {
464	      this.unenforceable.set(registration, { capability, reason })
465	      return () => { this.unenforceable.delete(registration) }
466	    }, `read-barrier unenforceable ${capability}`)
467	  }
468	
469	  /**
470	   * Why one capability that cannot be confined in-process must not start for a
471	   * session, or `undefined` when it may. Every start of such a capability asks
472	   * here, so the refusal is decided in the operation that would open the paths.
473	   * @param capability - the capability about to start.
474	   * @param session - the session it would start for; absent for an agentless call.
475	   * @returns the exact refusal from {@link startRefusalMessage}, or undefined.
476	   */
477	  startRefusal(capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability, session: Session | undefined): string | undefined {
478	    if (this.isolationClaim === 'none') return undefined
479	    if (this.roleOf(session) !== 'implementer') return undefined
480	    return startRefusalMessage(capability, this.isolationClaim)
481	  }
482	
483	  /**
484	   * Record what a preset roster composed for one agent. A declared role
485	   * outranks a reservation, because only the composition knows what was
486	   * actually mounted; a preset that declares none leaves the reservation to
487	   * decide. The roster is the only caller: nothing a session itself runs may
488	   * raise its own role.
489	   * @param agent - the agent whose composition was resolved.
490	   * @param composition - the preset id and the role it declared, if any.
491	   */
492	  declareComposition(agent: Agent, composition: ReadBarrierComposition): void {
493	    this.compositions.set(agent.id, composition)
494	  }
495	
496	  /**
497	   * Resolve the complete policy for one capability call. A session whose preset
498	   * declared a role holds that role; otherwise a session holding a reservation
499	   * is the implementer, and every other session and every agentless call is
500	   * unrestricted.
501	   * @param request - the calling session, when there is one.
502	   * @returns the role, the barrier root, and every denied directory.
503	   */
504	  resolve(request: ReadBarrierRequest = {}): ReadBarrierPolicy {
505	    return {
506	      role: this.roleOf(request.session),
507	      root: this.root,
508	      denied: [...new Set([this.root, ...this.configuredDenyRoots, ...this.protectedRoots.values()])],
509	    }
510	  }
511	
512	  /** The role one session holds: the preset's declaration first, then the reservation. */
513	  private roleOf(session: Session | undefined): ReadBarrierRole {
514	    if (session === undefined) return 'unrestricted'
515	    const declared = this.compositions.get(session.id)?.role
516	    if (declared !== undefined) return declared
517	    return this.reservations.has(session.id) ? 'implementer' : 'unrestricted'
518	  }
519	
520	  /**
521	   * One entry per path-opening capability: `denied-at-executor` when the
522	   * capability registered enforcement — through {@link enforce}, or through
523	   * {@link enforceByRefusal} under a `process` or `host` claim — `unenforced`
524	   * when it is composed without one, and `not-composed` when this composition
525	   * does not have it. An `unenforced` entry carries the reason whenever a
526	   * registration supplied one.
527	   * @returns the enforcement census in the fixed capability order.
528	   */
529	  enforcementCensus(): ReadBarrierEnforcementEntry[] {
530	    const enforced = new Set(this.enforcing.values())
531	    const refusing = new Set(this.refusing.values())
532	    const reasons = new Map([...this.unenforceable.values()].map(entry => [entry.capability, entry.reason]))
533	    return Object.entries(ENFORCED_CAPABILITY_SERVICES).map(([name, service]) => {
534	      const capability = name as ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability
535	      if (enforced.has(capability)) return { capability, state: 'denied-at-executor' as const }
536	      if (refusing.has(capability)) {
537	        return this.isolationClaim === 'none'
538	          ? { capability, state: 'unenforced' as const, reason: unclaimedRefusalReason(this.isolationClaim) }
539	          : { capability, state: 'denied-at-executor' as const }
540	      }
541	      // A recorded reason proves the capability is composed: only the
542	      // capability itself registers one, so it outranks the service lookup.
543	      const reason = reasons.get(capability)
544	      if (reason !== undefined) return { capability, state: 'unenforced' as const, reason }
545	      if (this.ctx.get(service) === undefined) return { capability, state: 'not-composed' as const }
546	      return { capability, state: 'unenforced' as const }
547	    })
548	  }
549	
550	  /**
551	   * One census entry per tool the agent's registry view resolves, with the
552	   * authorities each declares, sorted by tool name: the registry answers in
553	   * mount order, which follows concurrent Loader mounts and would make two runs
554	   * of one composition record different censuses.
555	   */
556	  private toolCensus(agent: Agent): ReadBarrierCensusEntry[] {
557	    const tools = agent.ctx.get('tools')
558	    if (tools === undefined) return []
559	    return tools.schemas(agent)
560	      .map(schema => ({
561	        name: schema.name,
562	        authority: [...tools.get(schema.name, agent)?.authority ?? []],
563	      }))
564	      // Two entries never share a name: the registry keys tools by it.
565	      .sort((left, right) => (left.name < right.name ? -1 : 1))
566	  }
567	
568	  /**
569	   * Append this session's composition census, and its host attestation when one
570	   * verifies, exactly once. Called before the loop composes the session's first
571	   * `request/header`, so the census is durable before any tool schema reaches a
572	   * model.
573	   */
574	  private recordScope(agent: Agent): void {
575	    if (this.censused.has(agent.id)) return
576	    this.censused.add(agent.id)
577	    const composition = this.compositions.get(agent.id)
578	    const scope: ReadBarrierScope = {
579	      version: READ_BARRIER_SCOPE_VERSION,
580	      role: this.roleOf(agent.session),
581	      ...composition === undefined ? {} : { presetId: composition.presetId },
582	      root: this.root,
583	      denied: this.resolve({ session: agent.session }).denied,
584	      census: this.toolCensus(agent),
585	      enforcement: this.enforcementCensus(),
586	    }
587	    agent.session.append('read-barrier/scope', scope)
588	    const attestation = this.verifiedAttestation()
589	    /* v8 ignore start -- only a file owned by another operating-system account reaches this append,
590	       which an unprivileged test process cannot create; `attestationProblem` covers every decision
591	       the record depends on. */
592	    if (attestation !== undefined) agent.session.append('read-barrier/attestation', attestation)
593	    /* v8 ignore stop */
594	  }
595	
596	  /**
597	   * Verify the configured host attestation file.
598	   * @returns the record to append, or undefined when no file is configured, it
599	   * cannot be read, or it does not prove another account owns it.
600	   */
601	  private verifiedAttestation(): ReadBarrierAttestation | undefined {
602	    const path = this.hostAttestation
603	    if (path === undefined) return undefined
604	    let file: AttestationFile
605	    try {
606	      const stats = statSync(path)
607	      file = {
608	        uid: stats.uid,
609	        mode: stats.mode,
610	        isFile: stats.isFile(),
611	        sha256: createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex'),
612	      }
613	    } catch {
614	      // An absent or unreadable attestation file is simply no attestation: the
615	      // claim it would have supported is refused instead of the run failing.
616	      this.ctx.logger.warn(`read-barrier: host attestation ${path} cannot be read; no certificate may claim host isolation`)
617	      return undefined
618	    }
619	    const problem = attestationProblem(file, process.geteuid?.())
620	    /* v8 ignore start -- the verifying arm needs a file owned by another operating-system account,
621	       which an unprivileged test process cannot create; `attestationProblem` covers every decision
622	       this arm depends on. */
623	    if (problem === undefined) {
624	      return { version: READ_BARRIER_ATTESTATION_VERSION, path, owner: file.uid, sha256: file.sha256 }
625	    }
626	    /* v8 ignore stop */
627	    this.ctx.logger.warn(`read-barrier: host attestation ${path} ${problem}; no certificate may claim host isolation`)
628	    return undefined
629	  }
630	
631	  /**
632	   * Register this agent's authority guard on its own scope, so a tool
633	   * registered into the agent's layer after its preset mounted is refused at
634	   * execution even though no composition audit saw it.
635	   */
636	  private installGuard(agent: Agent): void {
637	    // Registered through the AGENT's context: `tools.guard()` scopes the effect
638	    // to the caller's context, so the guard covers exactly this agent and
639	    // unwinds with it.
640	    agent.ctx.get('tools')?.guard(execution => this.guardExecution(agent, execution))
641	  }
642	
643	  /** Deny one execution whose definition carries an authority this session's role forbids. */
644	  private guardExecution(agent: Agent, execution: Readonly<ToolExecution>): string | undefined {
645	    const definition = agent.ctx.get('tools')?.get(execution.name, agent)
646	    const denied = deniedAuthority(this.roleOf(agent.session), definition?.authority)
647	    return denied === undefined ? undefined : authorityDenialMessage(execution.name, denied)
648	  }
649	
650	  /**
651	   * Decide whether the policy denies reading one resolved target. Each denied
652	   * directory is canonicalized through the filesystem seam immediately before
653	   * its containment test, so an ancestor symlink swapped since the target was
654	   * resolved is caught. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied.
655	   * @param policy - the policy {@link resolve} returned for this call.
656	   * @param target - the already-resolved target the caller is about to read.
657	   * @returns true when the read must be refused.
658	   */
659	  async denies(policy: ReadBarrierPolicy, target: FsTarget): Promise<boolean> {
660	    for (const denied of deniedReadRoots(policy)) {
661	      let directory: FsTarget
662	      try {
663	        directory = await this.ctx.fs.resolve(denied)
664	      } catch {
665	        // A denied directory the backend cannot resolve leaves containment
666	        // undecidable, and an undecidable read fails closed.
667	        return true
668	      }
669	      if (this.ctx.fs.contains(directory, target)) return true
670	    }
671	    return false
672	  }
673	
674	  /**
675	   * Append the durable record of one refusal. The barrier owns the write so
676	   * every seam that refuses produces the same evidence.
677	   * @param session - the refused session, whose log receives the record.
678	   * @param policy - the policy that refused, supplying the role and root.
679	   * @param capability - the seam that refused the read.
680	   * @param target - the refused target, supplying the model-facing path.
681	   * @returns the payload exactly as it was appended.
682	   */
683	  recordDenial(
684	    session: Session,
685	    policy: ReadBarrierPolicy,
686	    capability: ReadBarrierCapability,
687	    target: FsTarget,
688	  ): ReadBarrierDenial {
689	    const denial: ReadBarrierDenial = {
690	      version: READ_BARRIER_DENIED_VERSION,
691	      role: policy.role,
692	      capability,
693	      displayPath: target.displayPath,
694	      root: policy.root,
695	    }
696	    session.append('read-barrier/denied', denial)
697	    return denial
698	  }
699	}
700	
701	export default ReadBarrierService
702

# The `minimal` agent preset: a fixed-prompt, two-tool coding-agent composition.
#
# The persona is the complete system prompt, so global identity, Web orientation,
# tool guidance, and later assembly listeners cannot add prompt text. Runtime
# context snapshots are suppressed for this preset, and the model composes only
# persistent `bash` and `str_replace_editor`. Context compaction is absent.

- id: persona
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
  config:
    text: You are a helpful software engineer assistant.
    complete: true
    includeRuntimeContext: false

# The PTY registry is an agent-owned service, so it lives in an entry-local
# realm. The backend still consumes the host sandbox policy and subprocess
# implementation, while the tool registers into this agent's scoped catalog.
- id: persistent-shell
  name: cordis:group
  group: true
  isolate:
    terminals: true
  config:
    - id: pty
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal'

    - id: terminal-bash
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal-bash'
      config:
        timeoutMs: 300000

    - id: persistent-bash
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash-persistent'
      config:
        timeoutMs: 300000
        description: |-
          Run commands in a bash shell
          * When invoking this tool, the contents of the "command" parameter does NOT need to be XML-escaped.
          * You don't have access to the internet via this tool.
          * You do have access to a mirror of common linux and python packages via apt and pip.
          * State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user.
          * To inspect a particular line range of a file, e.g. lines 10-25, try 'sed -n 10,25p /path/to/the/file'.
          * Please avoid commands that may produce a very large amount of output.
          * Please run long lived commands in the background, e.g. 'sleep 10 &' or start a server in the background.

# The bare local filesystem shadows the host's sandboxed provider only for this
# preset. The editor shares that realm and requires absolute paths.
- id: filesystem
  name: cordis:group
  group: true
  isolate:
    fs: true
  config:
    - id: fs-local
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'
      config:
        cwd: !!js process.env.DSH_CWD ?? process.cwd()

    - id: str-replace-editor
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-str-replace-editor'
      config:
        maxOutputChars: 16000
=== code agent.cordis.yml ===
# The `code` agent preset: the standard coding agent, presented as Code Mode.
#
# Everything in `standard` is here unchanged. What is added is the `tool-presentation`
# row: instead of one tool call per action, the model writes a TypeScript
# program against a generated SDK and `run_code` executes it, so a sequence
# that would be five round trips becomes one.
#
# The registry itself stays on the host plane — the agent loop's scheduler and
# the API proxy's presenters are its consumers — so what this preset owns is
# the PRESENTATION of that registry for this agent alone. Native sessions run
# beside this one in the same process, each seeing its own catalog.
#
# This file is an AGENT-PLANE composition. It is mounted under one agent's
# scope context, so every tool and prompt section it registers belongs to that
# session alone. The host composition (`base.cordis.yml` + `web.cordis.yml`)
# keeps everything a preset must not own: the registries themselves, the
# sandbox and approval stack, persistence, and the model route.
#
# A service row here MUST sit inside a group carrying an `isolate` realm.
# Without one it publishes into the root realm, where it is process-global
# rather than per-session and the second session mounting this preset collides
# with the first; `dsh-agent-presets` rejects that at mount. `true` means an
# entry-local realm — one private instance per mounted session, which is the
# default this deployment wants. A shared label would instead pool one instance
# across every session naming it.

# ── identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The preset's own persona, shadowing the deployment default for this agent.
# `{{model}}` and `{{cwd}}` resolve from the agent's own route and workspace.
- id: persona
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
  config:
    text: >-
      You are a coding agent powered by the {{model}} model. Your working directory is {{cwd}}.

- id: agent-instructions
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
  config:
    maxBytes: 65536

# ── shell ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# `shell-env` stays in the HOST composition: `apps/cli/src/web.ts` injects it to
# publish `DSH_WEB_URL`/`DSH_WEB_MODE`, and a host row that injects a service is
# the criterion for host-plane ownership — injection resolves before any session
# exists, so there is no agent to key by. Behind a preset realm those variables
# never reached the model's shell at all. Both shell tools consume the host
# registry from here; their executors (`bash-sandbox`/`pwsh-sandbox`) are
# host-plane too.
- id: tool-bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
  disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'

- id: tool-pwsh
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
  disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'

# ── filesystem ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Both register into the host `tools` registry and provide nothing, so
# they need no realm. The `fs` service and its policy stay in the host.
- id: tool-fs
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'

- id: tool-fs-search
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
  config:
    sampleOverCapGlobResults: false

# ── background jobs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Only the model-facing controls. The task REGISTRY stays on the host plane:
# its producers sit outside any realm this file could put it in — `tool-bash`
# above resolves it with `ctx.get`, and an entry-local realm here is invisible
# to every sibling row, so `run_in_background` would answer "background jobs
# unavailable" while these controls sat in the catalog. The registry is keyed by
# owning agent anyway, so one host instance serves every session. What a preset
# chooses is whether its agent can collect and stop background work at all.
- id: tool-jobs
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'

# ── skills ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The skill REGISTRY lives in the host composition and is layered per scope:
# these rows register into THIS preset's layer of it, so they need no realm.
# `skill-filesystem` contributes local-root discovery for agents on this preset, and
# `tool-skill` gives them the catalog and loader; the merged catalog also
# carries whatever the deployment registered globally (repository plugins).
- id: skill-filesystem
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'

- id: tool-skill
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'

# ── goals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Only the model-facing tool. The goal SERVICE, its session driver, and the
# `/goal` command stay on the host plane: the Gateway serves the goal domain as
# Remote endpoints whose receiver comes from a generated descriptor, so it
# resolves `goals` on the host and an entry-local realm here would hide it. The
# registry is keyed by session anyway, so one host instance serves every
# session. What a preset chooses is whether its agent can call the goal tool.
- id: tool-goal
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'

# ── plan mode ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Plan state is per-agent by nature, so an entry-local realm is not a
# workaround here — it is the correct lifetime.
- id: planning
  name: cordis:group
  group: true
  isolate:
    planMode: true
  config:
    - id: plan-mode
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
      config:
        section: |
              You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until exit_plan_mode succeeds or the user switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

              Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

              The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

              Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

              Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

              When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.

# ── compaction ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# `compaction-basic` reads `toolResultPrune` through `ctx.get`, so the pruner must
# share this realm rather than sit outside it.
#
# `tokenMeter` is deliberately NOT in this realm: the meter stays on the HOST
# plane, and the rows here resolve that one instance. It takes no configuration,
# keys every fold by Session, and owns the context-meter projection units the
# browser reads for every session — behind a realm those units would come and go
# with whichever presets happen to be mounted. What a preset chooses is whether
# its agent compacts at all, which is `compaction-basic` below.
- id: compaction
  name: cordis:group
  group: true
  isolate:
    compaction: true
    toolResultPruner: true
  config:
    - id: compaction-basic
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'

    - id: command-compact
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

    - id: tool-result-pruner
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
      config:
        thresholdChars: 8192
        headChars: 4096
        tailChars: 1024

# ── delegation and workflows ────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The `subagents` registry and its spawn/fork backends live in the HOST
# composition: the registry is a process singleton whose cross-session queries
# the api-proxy serves to the browser, and a provider name may only be
# registered once. This preset contributes the delegation TOOLS, which resolve
# that host registry.
#
# `workflows` is different — nothing outside an agent reads it — so every row
# that reaches it shares one entry-local realm here, and a consumer left
# outside would resolve a host registry this preset does not populate.
- id: delegation
  name: cordis:group
  group: true
  isolate:
    workflowEngine: true
  config:
    - id: tool-subagent-control
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'

    - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'

    - id: tool-subagent
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
      config:
        provider: spawn
        toolName: subagent
        backgroundMode: continuable

    - id: tool-subagent-fork
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
      config:
        provider: fork
        toolName: subagent_fork
        backgroundMode: continuable

    # Product providers are host-plane singletons. Copy this preset, then
    # remove `disabled` from either ordinary tool row to expose that product
    # only to agents composed from the copy.
    - id: tool-subagent-codex
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
      disabled: true
      config:
        provider: codex
        toolName: subagent_codex
        enableRunInBackground: false
        maxDepth: provider-managed

    - id: tool-subagent-claude-code
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
      disabled: true
      config:
        provider: claude-code
        toolName: subagent_claude_code
        enableRunInBackground: false
        maxDepth: provider-managed

    - id: workflow-worker-thread
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread'
      config:
        provider: spawn

    - id: tool-workflow
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'

    - id: tool-ralph
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph'
      config:
        subagentProvider: spawn
        maxRounds: 64

# ── remaining model-facing rows ─────────────────────────────────────────────

- id: tool-ask-user
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'

- id: tool-todo
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
  config:
    allowParallelInProgress: true

# The `web` service and its search provider stay in the host composition; only
# the model-facing tool is per-session.
- id: tool-web
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
  config:
    fetch: false
    searchTimeoutMs: 60000

# ── presentation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Code Mode for this agent alone. The row waits for the host's `codeRuntime`
# rather than assuming it: a deployment that composes no TypeScript runtime
# fails this preset at mount, naming this id, instead of at the first request.
- id: tool-presentation
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-tool-presentation'
  config:
    mode: code

1	/**
2	 * A preset's display metadata: the name and description a picker shows.
3	 *
4	 * It lives in its own file because the composition is a top-level list of
5	 * plugin rows — YAML cannot carry sibling keys beside it, and faking a
6	 * metadata row would hand the Loader something to load. Keeping it separate
7	 * also keeps the composition exactly what its name says: a Cordis file the
8	 * loader owns and the cordis preset can author.
9	 *
10	 * The file carries display text and one authority claim. `id` is the directory
11	 * name and `trust` comes from the root a preset was discovered under, so
12	 * neither is writable here — otherwise a locally authored preset could claim to
13	 * be a shipped one.
14	 *
15	 * Every read failure degrades to no metadata. A preset whose display text is
16	 * missing, malformed, or unreadable still mounts: presentation is not a
17	 * capability, and a broken name must never become an agent that cannot start.
18	 * The same holds for `role`: an unrecognised value is no declaration, which
19	 * leaves the composition exactly as unrestricted as it is without the key.
20	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/metadata
21	 */
22	
23	import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
24	import { join } from 'node:path'
25	import yaml from 'js-yaml'
26	import type { ReadBarrierRole } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier/types'
27	
28	/** The optional display-metadata file beside a preset's composition. */
29	export const METADATA_FILE = 'preset.yml'
30	
31	/** Every role a preset may declare for the sessions it composes. */
32	export const PRESET_ROLES: readonly ReadBarrierRole[] = ['implementer', 'validator', 'unrestricted']
33	
34	/** Display text and the one authority claim a preset may publish about itself. */
35	export interface PresetMetadata {
36	  /** Human-facing name; falls back to the preset id when absent. */
37	  readonly name?: string
38	  /** One sentence on what this preset is for. */
39	  readonly description?: string
40	  /**
41	   * Position within its group; lower comes first. A preset that declares
42	   * none sorts after every preset that does, then by id — so the shipped set
43	   * can read in capability order while authored ones stay alphabetical.
44	   */
45	  readonly order?: number
46	  /**
47	   * Read-barrier role every session composed from this preset holds; absent
48	   * means `unrestricted`, which is what every preset without the key declares.
49	   * It is the one authority claim this file carries, so a `user`-trust preset
50	   * declaring `validator` is broken rather than mounted, and an `implementer`
51	   * preset composing a tool that carries an authority is refused at mount.
52	   */
53	  readonly role?: ReadBarrierRole
54	}
55	
56	/** A non-empty trimmed string, or undefined for anything else. */
57	function text(value: unknown): string | undefined {
58	  if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined
59	  const trimmed = value.trim()
60	  return trimmed === '' ? undefined : trimmed
61	}
62	
63	/** A declared role, or undefined for anything outside the vocabulary. */
64	function role(value: unknown): ReadBarrierRole | undefined {
65	  return PRESET_ROLES.find(candidate => candidate === value)
66	}
67	
68	/**
69	 * Read one preset directory's display metadata.
70	 *
71	 * Absent, unparsable, and wrongly-shaped files are all the same answer —
72	 * empty metadata — because the caller renders a picker, not a diagnostic.
73	 * @param directory - the preset directory.
74	 * @returns the display text the preset published, possibly empty.
75	 */
76	export async function readPresetMetadata(directory: string): Promise<PresetMetadata> {
77	  let raw: string
78	  try {
79	    raw = await readFile(join(directory, METADATA_FILE), 'utf8')
80	  } catch {
81	    // Absent is the common case: metadata is optional and most presets,
82	    // including every one authored by duplicating another, carry none.
83	    return {}
84	  }
85	  let parsed: unknown
86	  try {
87	    parsed = yaml.load(raw)
88	  } catch {
89	    // Malformed display text is not worth failing discovery over; the picker
90	    // falls back to the id, and the composition still mounts.
91	    return {}
92	  }
93	  if (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)) return {}
94	  const record = parsed as Record<string, unknown>
95	  const name = text(record.name)
96	  const description = text(record.description)
97	  const order = typeof record.order === 'number' && Number.isFinite(record.order)
98	    ? record.order
99	    : undefined
100	  const declaredRole = role(record.role)
101	  return {
102	    ...name === undefined ? {} : { name },
103	    ...description === undefined ? {} : { description },
104	    ...order === undefined ? {} : { order },
105	    ...declaredRole === undefined ? {} : { role: declaredRole },
106	  }
107	}
108	
109	/**
110	 * Render display metadata as the file's contents.
111	 *
112	 * Absent fields are omitted rather than written empty, so a preset with no
113	 * description does not ship a key that reads as an intentional blank.
114	 * @param metadata - the display text to store.
115	 * @returns the YAML document, or undefined when there is nothing to store.
116	 */
117	export function renderPresetMetadata(metadata: PresetMetadata): string | undefined {
118	  const name = text(metadata.name)
119	  const description = text(metadata.description)
120	  const { order } = metadata
121	  const declaredRole = role(metadata.role)
122	  if (name === undefined && description === undefined && order === undefined && declaredRole === undefined) {
123	    return undefined
124	  }
125	  return yaml.dump({
126	    ...name === undefined ? {} : { name },
127	    ...description === undefined ? {} : { description },
128	    ...order === undefined ? {} : { order },
129	    ...declaredRole === undefined ? {} : { role: declaredRole },
130	  }, { lineWidth: -1 })
131	}
