397	/**
398	 * The configured channels of one case whose observed value disagrees with the
399	 * case's expected digest, in the canonical channel order the log records.
400	 * @param body - the case that ran.
401	 * @param result - what the candidate produced.
402	 * @param scope - the absolute `treeScope` directory, absent for a check that declares none.
403	 * @returns the mismatching channels; empty when the case passed.
404	 */
405	async function caseMismatches(
406	  body: CheckCase,
407	  result: ShellRunResult,
408	  scope: string | undefined,
409	): Promise<CheckCaseChannel[]> {
410	  const { normalizers } = body.comparator
411	  const mismatched = new Set<CheckCaseChannel>()
412	  for (const channel of body.comparator.channels) {
413	    switch (channel) {
414	      case 'exit':
415	        if (result.exitCode !== body.expected.exitCode) mismatched.add(channel)
416	        break
417	      case 'stdout':
418	        if (streamMismatch(result.stdout, body.expected.stdoutSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
419	        break
420	      case 'stderr':
421	        if (streamMismatch(result.stderr, body.expected.stderrSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
422	        break
423	      case 'tree':
424	        // Authoring requires a treeScope for every check whose cases compare the tree.
425	        if (await hashDirectory(scope as string, normalizers) !== body.expected.treeSha256) mismatched.add(channel)
426	        break
427	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- CheckCaseChannel is closed and every member is handled above */
428	      default:
429	        return assertNever(channel)
430	    }
431	  }
432	  return CHECK_CASE_CHANNELS.filter(channel => mismatched.has(channel))
433	}

435	/** One rendered cluster with the check facts its line names. */
436	interface RenderedCluster extends DirectiveCluster {
437	  readonly outcome: string
438	  readonly total: number
439	  readonly weightTotal: number
440	  readonly exitClass: CaseExitClass
441	}
442	
443	/** Group one cased check's failed cases by the channels that disagreed and how the candidate ended. */
444	function clustersOf(check: StandardCheck, result: CheckResult): RenderedCluster[] {
445	  const cases = result.cases
446	  /* v8 ignore next -- only a cased result reaches here, and a cased result carries its tally */
447	  if (cases === undefined) return []
448	  const clusters = new Map<string, RenderedCluster>()
449	  for (const failed of cases.failed) {
450	    const key = `${failed.exitClass}|${failed.channels.join(',')}`
451	    const existing = clusters.get(key)
452	    clusters.set(key, {
453	      checkId: result.checkId,
454	      channels: failed.channels,
455	      count: (existing?.count ?? 0) + 1,
456	      weight: (existing?.weight ?? 0) + failed.weight,
457	      outcome: check.outcome,
458	      total: cases.total,
459	      weightTotal: cases.weightTotal,
460	      exitClass: failed.exitClass,
461	    })
462	  }
463	  return [...clusters.values()]
464	}

466	/**
467	 * One directive per failed run. A cased check contributes one line per failure
468	 * cluster, naming its authored outcome, the cluster's count and weight, the
469	 * channels that disagreed, and how the candidate ended — never a case body, an
470	 * expected digest, or a byte of captured output. A check without cases
471	 * contributes its recorded evidence line.
472	 * @param failures - the run's failing results, in check order.
473	 * @param checks - the standard's active checks, supplying each outcome text.
474	 * @param maxChars - bound of the rendered detail.
475	 * @returns the directive, carrying `clusters` when a cased check failed.
476	 */
477	function describeFailures(
478	  failures: readonly CheckResult[],
479	  checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
480	  maxChars: number,
481	): DirectiveRequest {
482	  const lines: string[] = []
483	  const clusters: DirectiveCluster[] = []
484	  for (const failure of failures) {
485	    const check = checks.find(candidate => candidate.id === failure.checkId)
486	    if (check === undefined || failure.cases === undefined) {
487	      lines.push(failure.evidence)
488	      continue
489	    }
490	    for (const cluster of clustersOf(check, failure)) {
491	      clusters.push({ checkId: cluster.checkId, channels: cluster.channels, count: cluster.count, weight: cluster.weight })
492	      lines.push(`${cluster.outcome}: ${cluster.count} of ${cluster.total} cases failed (weight ${cluster.weight} of ${cluster.weightTotal}); mismatching channels: ${cluster.channels.join(', ')}; ${EXIT_PHRASE[cluster.exitClass]}`)
493	    }
494	  }
495	  return {
496	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
497	    detail: bound(lines.map((line, index) => `${index + 1}. ${line}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
498	    ...clusters.length === 0 ? {} : { clusters },
499	  }
500	}

502	/**
503	 * The one directive a tampered attempt issues. A digest comparison knows that
504	 * the check-owned set changed and nothing else, so the text names neither a
505	 * path nor a check: it states that the measurement is void and that the run is
506	 * over. Pinned verbatim by the runner README and the `read-barrier-tamper`
507	 * snapshot.
508	 */
509	const TAMPER_DIRECTIVE: DirectiveRequest = {
510	  rootCause: 'the files this task is measured with were modified during the attempt',
511	  detail: 'Those files belong to the validator: the task is to make them pass, never to change them. This run is void and no certificate can follow it.',
512	}
513	
514	/** The evidence every check of a tampered attempt records, since none of them ran. */
515	const TAMPER_EVIDENCE = 'not executed: the files this task is measured with were modified during the attempt'
516	
517	/** The validator's follow-up turn after a failed run; the text is pinned by the runner README and its e2e. */
518	function followupText(directive: DirectiveRequest): string {
519	  return `<validation_failed>\n${directive.rootCause}\n${directive.detail}\nContinue working on the task; the validator runs again when you stop.\n</validation_failed>`
520	}

522	/** Sum the usage of every assistant message in a session log. */
523	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
524	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
525	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
526	  ))
527	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
528	  const total: TokenUsage = {
529	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
530	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
531	  }
532	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
533	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
534	      const value = step[key]
535	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
536	    })
537	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
538	  }
539	  return total
540	}

542	/** Environment runner (`ctx.environmentRuns`): one registered environment as one validated session. */
543	export class EnvironmentRunner extends Service {
544	  static inject = ['environments', 'agents', 'agentDefaultModel', 'goals', 'completionStandards', 'shell', 'sessions']
545	
546	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
547	    isolation: z.union(['none', 'process', 'host'] as const).required(),
548	    maxAttempts: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
549	    maxGoalRounds: z.natural().min(1),
550	    checkTimeoutMs: z.natural().min(1),
551	    evidenceMaxChars: z.natural().min(1).default(2000),
552	    maxFailedCases: z.natural().min(1).default(20),
553	  })
554	
555	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
556	
557	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
558	    super(ctx, 'environmentRuns')
559	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
560	  }

562	  /**
563	   * Run one environment as one fresh session and validate it.
564	   * @param request - environment id, absolute workspace directory, optional model route, repetition, group, district, and abort signal.
565	   * @returns the stamp, the attempts, the certificate when one run passed, and the accumulated usage.
566	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} for an unknown environment, an unusable
567	   *   workspace or fixture, an implementer that replaced the goal, or a lost standard.
568	   */
569	  async run(request: EnvironmentRunRequest): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
570	    const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(request.environment)
571	    if (definition === undefined) {
572	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`environment "${request.environment}" is not registered`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT')
573	    }
574	    const fixtureSha256 = await prepareWorkspace(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
575	    const model = request.model ?? this.defaultModel()
576	    const stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp = {
577	      kind: 'environment/run',
578	      version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
579	      environmentId: definition.id,
580	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
581	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
582	      ...environmentContentHashes(definition, fixtureSha256),
583	      repetition: request.repetition ?? 0,
584	      ...request.group === undefined ? {} : { group: request.group },
585	      ...request.district === undefined ? {} : { district: request.district },
586	      model,
587	      isolation: this.resolved.isolation,
588	    }
589	    const handle = await this.ctx.agents.create({
590	      sessionId: SessionId(`environment-${randomUUID()}`),
591	      meta: { cwd: request.workspace },
592	      agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
593	      ...request.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: request.signal },
594	      setup: (agentCtx) => {
595	        installModelSelection(agentCtx, { current: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model }, assembled: undefined })
596	      },
597	    })
598	    try {
599	      return await this.drive(handle.agent, definition, stamp, request)
600	    } finally {
601	      await handle.dispose()
602	    }
603	  }
604	
605	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
606	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
607	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
608	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
609	  }

611	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
612	  private async drive(
613	    agent: Agent,
614	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
615	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
616	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
617	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
618	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
619	    await agent.whenIdle()
620	    const runDirectory = await this.reserve(agent, definition)
621	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
622	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {
623	      objective: definition.task.prompt,
624	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
625	    })
626	    goals.disarm(agent)
627	    const authored = completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
628	    // Authorship validated every case against the reference it carries and kept
629	    // the reference alone; the bodies stay here, for the reservation and the
630	    // per-case execution.
631	    const bodies = new Map(definition.checks.flatMap(check => (
632	      check.caseBodies === undefined ? [] : [[check.id, check.caseBodies] as const]
633	    )))
634	    const immutable = definition.task.immutable ?? []
635	    // Stock the reservation and digest the check-owned set before the
636	    // implementer's first turn: that digest is what every later attempt is
637	    // compared against.
638	    await materializeChecks(runDirectory, authored, bodies)
639	    let checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
640	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
641	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
642	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
643	    try {
644	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
645	        await this.deliver(agent, prompt)
646	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
647	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
648	        if (await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable) !== checkOwned) {
649	          attempts.push(await this.recordTamper(agent, standard, ref, request.workspace, attempt))
650	          break
651	        }
652	        const treeHash = await restoreFixture(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
653	        const scripts = await materializeChecks(runDirectory, standard, bodies)
654	        // The validator just rewrote its own directory, so the set it now owns
655	        // is the baseline the next attempt must still find.
656	        checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
657	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request, scripts, bodies)
658	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
659	          executor: 'runner',
660	          treeHash,
661	        })
662	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
663	        if (outcome.certified) {
664	          certificate = outcome.certificate
665	          const current = goals.get(agent)
666	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
667	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')
668	          }
669	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
670	          break
671	        }
672	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, standard.checks, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)
673	        completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, directive)
674	        prompt = followupText(directive)
675	      }
676	    } finally {
677	      await sessions.flush(agent.session)
678	    }
679	    const usage = totalUsage(agent.session.events)
680	    return {
681	      environment: definition.id,
682	      sessionId: agent.id,
683	      stamp,
684	      attempts,
685	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
686	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
687	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
688	    }
689	  }

691	  /** Send one user turn to the implementer and wait for the whole agent to go idle. */
692	  private async deliver(agent: Agent, text: string): Promise<void> {
693	    agent.followup(createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text }], source: { kind: 'user' } }))
694	    await agent.whenIdle()

697	  /**
698	   * Record one attempt whose check-owned set changed under the validator. The
699	   * checks are not executed — the workspace no longer measures the task — so
700	   * every result records that, the run is recorded as `tampered` and certifies
701	   * nothing, and the implementer receives the tamper directive as its last
702	   * validation follow-up before the attempt loop ends.
703	   * @param agent - the implementer whose attempt this is.
704	   * @param standard - the standard the attempt would have measured.
705	   * @param ref - that standard's exact revision.
706	   * @param workspace - the run's workspace, digested as the attempt left it.
707	   * @param attempt - one-based attempt number.
708	   * @returns the attempt the report carries.
709	   */
710	  private async recordTamper(
711	    agent: Agent,
712	    standard: StandardView,
713	    ref: StandardRef,
714	    workspace: string,
715	    attempt: number,
716	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunAttempt> {
717	    const results: CheckResult[] = standard.checks.map(check => ({
718	      checkId: check.id,

720	      evidence: bound(TAMPER_EVIDENCE, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),

734	  private currentStandard(agent: Agent, goalId: GoalId): StandardView {
735	    const standard = this.ctx.completionStandards.get(agent)
736	    if (standard === undefined || standard.goalId !== goalId) {

743	   * Reserve the run's validator-owned directory and stock what the checks read
744	   * from it. Without a composed barrier there is no reservation and the checks
745	   * run their instructions inline, exactly as the run's declared isolation says.
746	   * @param agent - the implementer agent this run drives.

751	    const barrier = this.ctx.get('readBarrier')
752	    if (barrier === undefined) return undefined

763	  /**
764	   * Run every active check in order through the shell executor rooted at the
765	   * workspace. A reserved check runs its script; an unreserved one runs its
766	   * instruction inline. A check that carries cases runs once per case and its
767	   * verdict follows the cases; every other check's verdict is its exit code.
768	   */
769	  private async execute(
770	    checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
771	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
772	    scripts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
773	    bodies: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly CheckCase[]>,
774	  ): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
775	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
776	    for (const check of checks) {
777	      const script = scripts.get(check.id)
778	      const command = script === undefined ? check.run : `. ${script}`
779	      const cases = bodies.get(check.id)
780	      if (cases === undefined) {
781	        const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(this.caseSpec(command, request))
782	        results.push({
783	          checkId: check.id,
784	          status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
785	          evidence: evidenceOf(result, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
786	        })
787	        continue
788	      }
789	      const run = await this.executeCases(check, cases, command, request)
790	      // One bounded list of named failures serves both the durable tally and
791	      // the evidence, so a run of hundreds of cases names the same subset twice.
792	      const named = run.failures.slice(0, this.resolved.maxFailedCases)
793	      results.push({
794	        checkId: check.id,
795	        status: run.passed === run.total ? 'pass' : 'fail',
796	        evidence: casedEvidenceOf(run, named, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
797	        cases: {
798	          passed: run.passed,
799	          total: run.total,
800	          weightPassed: run.weightPassed,
801	          weightTotal: run.weightTotal,
802	          failed: named.map(failure => ({
803	            id: failure.id,
804	            weight: failure.weight,
805	            channels: failure.channels,
806	            exitClass: failure.exitClass,
807	          })),
808	        },
809	      })
810	    }
811	    return results
812	  }

814	  /** Resolve one check or case command against the workspace and the run's cancellation. */
815	  private caseSpec(command: string, request: EnvironmentRunRequest, stdin?: string): ShellExecSpec {
816	    return this.ctx.shell.resolve({
817	      command,
818	      workdir: request.workspace,
819	      timeoutMs: this.resolved.checkTimeoutMs,
820	      signal: request.signal,
821	      ...stdin === undefined ? {} : { stdin },
822	    })

825	  /**
826	   * Run one cased check case by case: empty the check's `treeScope`, stage the
827	   * case's files, append its `argv` to the check's command, feed its `stdin`,
828	   * then compare every configured channel against the case's digest.
829	   */
830	  private async executeCases(
831	    check: StandardCheck,
832	    cases: readonly CheckCase[],
833	    command: string,
834	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
835	  ): Promise<CasedCheckRun> {
836	    const failures: CaseFailure[] = []
837	    let passedCases = 0
838	    let weightPassed = 0
839	    for (const body of cases) {
840	      const scope = check.treeScope === undefined ? undefined : join(request.workspace, check.treeScope)
841	      if (scope !== undefined) {
842	        await rm(scope, { recursive: true, force: true })
843	        await mkdir(scope, { recursive: true })
844	      }
845	      for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(body.input.files ?? {})) {
846	        const staged = join(request.workspace, path)
847	        await mkdir(dirname(staged), { recursive: true })
848	        await writeFile(staged, content)
849	      }
850	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(
851	        this.caseSpec([command, ...body.input.argv].join(' '), request, body.input.stdin),
852	      )
853	      const channels = await caseMismatches(body, result, scope)
854	      if (channels.length === 0) {
855	        passedCases += 1
856	        weightPassed += body.weight
857	        continue
858	      }
859	      failures.push({ id: body.id, weight: body.weight, channels, exitClass: exitClassOf(result), result })
860	    }
861	    return {
862	      passed: passedCases,
863	      total: cases.length,
864	      weightPassed,
865	      weightTotal: cases.reduce((sum, body) => sum + body.weight, 0),
866	      failures,
867	    }
868	  }

87	async function deepseekDefaultsServer(): Promise<DeepSeekDefaultsServer> {
88	  const requests: JsonObject[] = []
89	  const server = createServer((request: IncomingMessage, response: ServerResponse) => {
90	    let body = ''
91	    request.setEncoding('utf8')
92	    request.on('data', (chunk: string) => { body += chunk })
93	    request.on('end', () => {
94	      requests.push(JSON.parse(body) as JsonObject)
95	      response.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'text/event-stream' })
96	      let keepAlives = 3
97	      const write = (): void => {
98	        if (keepAlives-- > 0) {
99	          response.write(': keep-alive\n\n')
100	          setTimeout(write, 60)
101	          return
102	        }
103	        response.end([
104	          'data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"DEFAULTS_OK"}}]}',
105	          'data: {"choices":[{"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":3,"completion_tokens":1}}',
106	          'data: [DONE]',
107	          '',
108	        ].join('\n\n'))
109	      }
110	      setTimeout(write, 60)
111	    })
112	  })
113	  await new Promise<void>(resolve => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve))
114	  const address = server.address()
115	  if (address === null || typeof address === 'string') throw new Error('DeepSeek defaults snapshot server has no port')
116	  return {
117	    url: `http://127.0.0.1:${address.port}`,
118	    requests,
119	    close: () => new Promise(resolve => server.close(() => { resolve() })),
120	  }

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

# Replay counterpart to tests/fixtures/read-barrier-tamper/cordis.yml: the same
# runner composition with the committed model script in place of the fixture's
# scripted adapter, so the tamper directive the implementer receives is pinned
# without a key.
- id: llm-replay
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-replay'
  config:
    providers:
      - id: tamper-mock
        name: Replay
        models:
          - id: tamper-mock
            contextWindow: 128000

# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor (spawn/kill/output plumbing).
- id: subprocess
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'

- id: bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'

- id: goal
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'

- id: verification
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'

- id: environments
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'

- id: register-environment
  name: './tests/fixtures/read-barrier-tamper/register-environment.ts'

# The runner creates its own agent per run from this selection; the spine composes no agent of its own.
- id: agent-default-model
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
  config:
    provider: tamper-mock
    model: tamper-mock

- id: environment-runner
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
  config:
    isolation: none
    maxAttempts: 2
    evidenceMaxChars: 512

# Village rule: a composition that runs unattended sessions carries a session
# budget. The caps are far out of reach of the replayed route, so no run breaches them.
- id: budget-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
  config:
    maxTotalTokens: 5000000
    maxWallMs: 600000

- id: agent-spine
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-spine-demo'
  config:
    persona: 'Run the registered environment as a validated session.'
    workspaceContext: false

- id: persistence
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
  config:
    root: './.sessions'
    compression: none

- id: checkpoint-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy'

- id: trajectories

1 # Completion standards 2 3 English | [中文](verification.zh.md) 4 5 Types shared by the completion-standard service and its consumers. A standard is one executable check inventory per goal; a certificate is the durable record of one fully passing run under a stated isolation level, and goal completion of a measured goal is admitted only with a covering certificate. The [verification seams Agent Note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) owns the design; this page records the exact fields from [`packages/verification/verification/src/types.ts`](../../packages/verification/verification/src/types.ts). 6 7 ## Identity and checks 8 9 `StandardId` and `CheckId` are [branded ids](core.md#branded-ids). A caller mutates one exact standard revision through `StandardRef`; every durable mutation increments the revision. 10 11 ```ts type-equiv 12 /** Compare-and-set identity for one exact standard revision. */ 13 interface StandardRef { 14 /** Stable standard identity. */ 15 readonly id: StandardId 16 /** Positive revision; every durable mutation increments it. */ 17 readonly revision: number 18 } 19 ``` 20 21 A check states the outcome the task must establish and how a validator runs it; the implementer never reads it. 22 23 ```ts type-equiv 24 /** One executable check: the outcome it establishes and how a validator runs it. */ 25 interface StandardCheck { 26 /** Lower-kebab-case identity unique inside the owning standard. */ 27 readonly id: CheckId 28 /** Outcome the task must establish, stated without the implementation. */ 29 readonly outcome: string 30 /** Validator-owned execution instruction (command line or procedure). */ 31 readonly run: string 32 /** Reference to the check's case bodies; absent for a check whose verdict is its own exit code. */ 33 readonly cases?: CheckCasesRef 34 /** 35 * Normalized workspace-relative directory the `tree` channel digests, which 36 * the runner empties before each case that compares it. Present exactly when 37 * a case compares `tree`. 38 */ 39 readonly treeScope?: string 40 } 41 ``` 42 43 ## Weighted cases 44 45 A check may sample the candidate's behaviour case by case instead of reducing to one exit code. The durable log carries the reference; the bodies live in the validator's reservation, and `sha256` binds the two. 46 47 ```ts type-equiv 48 /** 49 * The durable reference to one check's case bodies. The bodies live in the 50 * validator's reservation, never in the session log; `sha256` binds the two. 51 */ 52 interface CheckCasesRef { 53 /** Number of cases the bodies hold. */ 54 readonly count: number 55 /** Sum of every case weight. */ 56 readonly weightTotal: number 57 /** SHA-256 hex of the canonical case bodies. */ 58 readonly sha256: string 59 } 60 ``` 61 62 ```ts type-equiv 63 /** One behavioural sample of a check: what the candidate is fed and what it must produce. */ 64 interface CheckCase { 65 /** Lower-kebab-case identity unique inside the owning check. */ 66 readonly id: CheckCaseId 67 /** Positive safe-integer share of the check's weight this case carries. */ 68 readonly weight: number 69 /** What the case feeds the candidate. */ 70 readonly input: CheckCaseInput 71 /** Digests the case's configured channels are compared against. */ 72 readonly expected: CheckCaseExpectation 73 /** Channels compared and the normalizers applied before comparison. */ 74 readonly comparator: CheckCaseComparator 75 } 76 ``` 77 78 ```ts type-equiv 79 /** 80 * Channel one case compares. `exit` is the candidate's exit code, `stdout` and 81 * `stderr` its captured bytes, and `tree` the work tree under the check's 82 * `treeScope` as the case left it. 83 */ 84 type CheckCaseChannel = 'exit' | 'stdout' | 'stderr' | 'tree' 85 ``` 86 87 The normalizer set is closed: every entry widens what counts as equal, so extending it is a design decision rather than a deployment choice. Each is a pure, idempotent function over the channel's bytes, applied in the comparator's order; [`packages/verification/verification`](../../packages/verification/verification/README.md#weighted-cases) states what each one does. 88 89 ```ts type-equiv 90 /** 91 * Pure byte function applied to a compared channel before it is digested, in 92 * the comparator's order. The set is closed: every normalizer widens what 93 * counts as equal, so a new one is a design decision rather than a 94 * deployment choice. 95 * 96 * - `crlf` rewrites every `\r\n` to `\n`. 97 * - `trailing-whitespace` drops spaces and tabs at the end of each line. 98 * - `blank-lines` drops leading and trailing blank lines and collapses each 99 * interior run of them to one. 100 * - `iso8601-timestamps` replaces each ISO-8601 timestamp with ``. 101 * - `temp-paths` replaces each temporary-directory prefix with ``. 102 * - `json-canonical` reserializes valid JSON with sorted keys and no 103 * insignificant whitespace, and leaves anything else unchanged. 104 */ 105 type CheckCaseNormalizer = 106 | 'crlf' 107 | 'trailing-whitespace' 108 | 'blank-lines' 109 | 'iso8601-timestamps' 110 | 'temp-paths' 111 | 'json-canonical' 112 ``` 113 114 A cased check's result carries the tally its verdict follows, and the run sums those tallies into one weighted pass rate. 115 116 ```ts type-equiv 117 /** Case tally of one executed check, present exactly for a check that carries cases. */ 118 interface CheckCaseResults { 119 /** Cases whose every configured channel matched. */ 120 readonly passed: number 121 /** Cases executed; equal to the check's `cases.count`. */ 122 readonly total: number 123 /** Summed weight of the passing cases. */ 124 readonly weightPassed: number 125 /** Summed weight of every case; equal to the check's `cases.weightTotal`. */ 126 readonly weightTotal: number 127 /** Failed cases, bounded by the executing runner; never longer than `total - passed`. */ 128 readonly failed: readonly FailedCheckCase[] 129 } 130 ``` 131 132 ```ts type-equiv 133 /** Weighted pass rate of one run, summed over the checks that carry cases. */ 134 interface RunParity { 135 /** Summed weight of every passing case of the run. */ 136 readonly weightPassed: number 137 /** Summed weight of every case of the run. */ 138 readonly weightTotal: number 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 `parity` rides the `verification/run` event and certifies nothing: a certificate still requires every case of every active check to pass. A directive crossing to the implementer carries only clusters, never a case body, an expected digest, or captured output. 143 144 ```ts type-equiv 145 /** 146 * One failure cluster of a directive: the failed cases of one check that 147 * disagreed on the same channels and ended the same way. It carries counts and 148 * weights only, never a case body, an expected digest, or captured output. 149 */ 150 interface DirectiveCluster { 151 /** Check whose cases the cluster groups. */ 152 readonly checkId: CheckId 153 /** Channels that disagreed, in the canonical `exit`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `tree` order. */ 154 readonly channels: readonly CheckCaseChannel[] 155 /** Cases in the cluster. */ 156 readonly count: number 157 /** Summed weight of the cluster's cases. */ 158 readonly weight: number 159 } 160 ``` 161 162 ## Certificates 163 164 A certificate covers exactly one standard revision and carries one passing result per active check, plus the isolation the run executed under: `none` (shared filesystem reach), `process` (in-process read policy only), or `host` (separate operating-system account or host). 165 166 ```ts type-equiv 167 /** Durable record of one fully passing run of the current standard. */ 168 interface VerificationCertificate { 169 /** Exact standard revision the run covered. */ 170 readonly standard: StandardRef 171 /** Goal the certified standard measures. */ 172 readonly goalId: GoalId 173 /** Isolation level the certified run executed under. */ 174 readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation 175 /** 176 * Executor of the certified run, copied from the `verification/run` this 177 * certificate cites. An `agent-reported` run is the implementer's own account 178 * of its checks, so it may certify only at `isolation: 'none'`. 179 */ 180 readonly executor: RunExecutor 181 /** One passing result per active check, in the standard's check order. */ 182 readonly results: readonly CheckResult[] 183 /** Epoch milliseconds of the certificate commit. */ 184 readonly recordedAt: number 185 } 186 ``` 187 188 The five durable events (`verification/standard`, `verification/relaxation`, `verification/run`, `verification/certificate`, `verification/directive`) are catalogued in [persistence-catalog.md](../persistence-catalog.md#verificationstandard--log-only); every executed run is recorded with the verdict its results and its caller's tamper report decide, and a certificate covers only a run whose verdict is `passed`. The `verification` session projection serves the current standard with its covering certificate. 189 190 ## The read barrier 191 192 Types the read barrier decides from, declared by [`packages/verification/read-barrier`](../../packages/verification/read-barrier/README.md). A session's role decides what it may read; a reservation is what makes a session the implementer. 193 194 ```ts type-equiv 195 /** 196 * Authority a session holds against the barrier. `implementer` is denied every 197 * directory the barrier owns; `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied 198 * nothing, and `unrestricted` is what a session holds without a reservation. 199 * Which directories a role may read is a security invariant, never a 200 * deployment choice. 201 */ 202 type ReadBarrierRole = 'implementer' | 'validator' | 'unrestricted' 203 ``` 204 205 ```ts type-equiv 206 /** 207 * Capability seam that refused one read. Each member names a seam that opens 208 * paths and can therefore decide a refusal in the operation that opens them. 209 */ 210 type ReadBarrierCapability = 'fs' | 'shell' | 'subprocess' | 'terminal' 211 ``` 212 213 ```ts type-equiv 214 /** Inputs that select the barrier policy for one capability call. */ 215 interface ReadBarrierRequest { 216 /** Calling session; its reservation decides the role. Absent means an agentless call. */ 217 session?: Session 218 } 219 ``` 220 221 ```ts type-equiv 222 /** 223 * The barrier's complete decision inputs for one session, resolved once per 224 * capability call. `denied` lists every directory the role may not read, 225 * canonicalized only at the moment of the containment test. 226 */ 227 interface ReadBarrierPolicy { 228 /** Authority the calling session holds. */ 229 readonly role: ReadBarrierRole 230 /** The barrier's own validator-owned root, always the first denied directory. */ 231 readonly root: string 232 /** Every denied directory: the root, the configured extras, and the registered ones. */ 233 readonly denied: readonly string[] 234 } 235 ``` 236 237 The barrier appends one `read-barrier/denied` event per refusal, catalogued in [persistence-catalog.md](../persistence-catalog.md#read-barrierdenied--log-only). 238 239 ```ts type-equiv 240 /** 241 * One refusal, as the `read-barrier/denied` session event carries it. 4	
5	The read barrier (`ctx.readBarrier`): the policy home for reads an implementer session must not perform, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. It owns one validator-owned directory tree, mints the per-run directory a validator stocks with what its checks execute, collects the directories other plugins register, resolves one policy per session, decides containment through the filesystem seam, records what each session composed, and verifies the host attestation a `host` isolation claim needs. It denies nothing by itself: each path-opening capability enforces the decision in the operation that opens paths, which is what [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier`](../../fs/fs-read-barrier/README.md) does for `ctx.fs`. The [read-barrier Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-read-barrier.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: read-barrier
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
12	  config:
13	    root: ~/.dsh/verification
14	    denyRoots:
15	      - /srv/evaluation/fixtures
16	    hostAttestation: /srv/attestation/run.json
17	    isolationClaim: process
18	```
19	
20	| Field | Meaning |
21	|---|---|
22	| `root` (default `<harness home>/verification`) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed directory the barrier owns. Created `0700` at load; an existing directory readable beyond its owner is rejected there, and so is a path that is not absolute after `~` expansion. |
23	| `denyRoots` (default `[]`) | Further absolute or `~`-prefixed directories denied alongside `root`, for directories no plugin registers through `protect()`. |
24	| `hostAttestation` (default none) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed file an external account writes. Without a file the barrier verified, no certificate may claim `host` isolation. |
25	| `isolationClaim` (default `none`) | The isolation this deployment intends its certificates to claim: `none`, `process`, or `host`. It decides only what a capability the harness cannot fence in-process does for an implementer session — refuse to start under `process` or `host`, run unenforced under `none`. It grants nothing; what a certificate may actually claim is decided by [`dsh-verification`](../verification/README.md) over the census below. |
26	
27	The denied set for a role is deliberately not a field, and neither are the authorities a role may hold: both are security invariants, not deployment choices. The service requires `fs`, because containment is decided through that seam rather than by parsing path strings.
28	
29	## Service contract
30	
31	`ctx.readBarrier.reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` owner-only, records that session as the `implementer`, and returns the absolute path; reserving the same session again returns the same directory. It is synchronous so the role is in force the moment the caller returns. A validator writes there what its checks execute — the standard snapshot, one script per check, any held-out fixture — so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. The reservation is dropped when the agent is disposed.
32	
33	`ctx.readBarrier.protect(path)` denies one more directory for as long as the registration lives and returns its disposer, so a plugin that owns a directory contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration. Two registrations of one path both hold; the directory leaves the denied set when the last is disposed.
34	
35	`ctx.readBarrier.enforce(capability)` records that one path-opening capability — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, or `workflow` — denies the barrier's directories in the operation that opens paths, for as long as the registration lives, and returns its disposer. A composed capability without one is `unenforced` in the census, and an isolation claim above `none` is refused while any such entry stands. [`enforceReadBarrier`](../../sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) is how each sandbox-consuming executor makes this call, so no capability claims an enforcement its own backend never applies.
36	
37	`ctx.readBarrier.enforceByRefusal(capability)` is its sibling for the executors this process cannot fence: a worker thread recovers the host process's privileges and an out-of-process agent brings its own tool stack, so neither can deny a read where it opens paths. The census follows `isolationClaim` — `denied-at-executor` under `process` or `host`, where `startRefusal` refuses every implementer start, and `unenforced` with that reason under `none`, where the capability runs and denies nothing.
38	
39	`ctx.readBarrier.cannotEnforce(capability, reason)` records that a composed capability cannot enforce on this host, with the reason the capability supplies — the backend that cannot express the denial, or a deployment mode that runs commands unconfined. The certificate refused over such a census names the reason instead of only the capability. An `enforce()` registration for the same capability outranks it.
40	
41	`ctx.readBarrier.startRefusal(capability, session)` answers the exact refusal a capability that cannot be confined in-process must return instead of starting, or `undefined` when it may start. Every start of such a capability asks here, so the refusal is decided in the operation that would open the paths. `startRefusalMessage(capability, claim)` owns the text.
42	
43	`deniedReadRoots(policy)` answers the directories a resolved policy actually denies its holder: every denied directory for an `implementer`, none for any other role. One place decides which roles the denied set binds, so a process runner filling its own denial and the in-process `denies()` test cannot disagree.
44	
45	`ctx.readBarrier.declareComposition(agent, { presetId, role })` records what a preset roster composed for one agent. A declared role outranks a reservation, because only the composition knows what was actually mounted; a preset that declares none leaves the reservation to decide. [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../preset/agent-presets/README.md) is the only caller: nothing a session itself runs may raise its own role.
46	
47	`ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied }`. A session whose preset declared a role holds that role; otherwise a session holding a reservation is the `implementer`, and every other session and every agentless call is `unrestricted`. `denied` lists the root first, then the configured extras, then each registration, without repeats.
48	
49	`ctx.readBarrier.denies(policy, target)` decides containment for an already-resolved `FsTarget`. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing. For an `implementer`, each denied directory is canonicalized through `ctx.fs.resolve` immediately before `ctx.fs.contains` tests it, so an ancestor symlink swapped since the target was resolved is caught; a directory the backend cannot resolve leaves containment undecidable and the read is denied.
50	
51	`ctx.readBarrier.recordDenial(session, policy, capability, target)` appends the log-only `read-barrier/denied` event — `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, with `capability` naming the seam that refused — and returns the payload it appended. The barrier owns the write so every refusing seam produces the same evidence; the path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the record adds evidence and no new disclosure.
52	
53	`deniedAuthority(role, authority)` answers the first authority a role may not hold. Every authority a [`ToolDefinition`](../../core/tools/README.md) declares is denied to an `implementer` and none to any other role, so an authority merged into `ToolAuthorityMap` later is denied by this same rule rather than by a list that would go stale. `authorityDenialMessage(tool, authority)` owns the text the guard returns.
54	
55	### The composition census
56	
57	Before a session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` carrying `{ version, role, presetId?, root, denied, census, enforcement }`. `census` is one `{ name, authority }` entry per tool the session's registry view resolves, sorted by tool name because registry order follows concurrent Loader mounts and would otherwise make two runs of one composition record different censuses; it makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability, valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`, in a fixed capability order; an `unenforced` entry carries the `reason` its capability recorded, when it recorded one. When a `hostAttestation` file is configured and verifies — a regular file owned by another operating-system account and unwritable by this one — the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/attestation` beside it, carrying `{ version, path, owner, sha256 }`. An absent or unverifiable file records nothing and logs a warning; the claim it would have supported is refused instead of the run failing.
58	
59	The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` on each agent's own context at `agent/created`, denying any execution whose definition carries an authority that session's role forbids. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission. The `mountPreset` audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards.
60	
61	The separately published `./invariant` companion rejects a refusal recorded for any role but `implementer`, one carrying an unknown payload version or capability, and one naming a different barrier root than the session's earlier records. It rejects a census of unknown version, one for an unknown role, one recording enforcement for a capability that opens no path or a decision outside the vocabulary, and a second census in one session; and an attestation of unknown version or with no file path.
62	
63	## Model Experience
64	
65	### Refused reads
66	
67	#### What the model sees
68	
69	Nothing this package renders. Its decision reaches the model only as the refusal the enforcing capability returns from the operation the model called: for `ctx.fs` reads that is [`dsh-fs-read-barrier`](../../fs/fs-read-barrier/README.md), which owns the exact message. No prompt section, tool schema, or tool description mentions the barrier, and a session that never reads a denied path cannot tell it is composed.
70	
71	#### Token effect
72	
73	Zero direct tokens. A refused read replaces the tool result the model would have received with the enforcing capability's short error, so a denial spends fewer tokens than the read it refused.
74	
75	#### KV Cache effect
76	
77	Append-only, and prefix-stable: the barrier adds nothing to the system prompt or to tool schemas, and its own events are log-only, so an existing reusable request prefix survives every refusal.
78	
79	### Refused starts
80	
81	#### What the model sees
82	
83	A model that delegates to an out-of-process subagent provider, or starts a worker-thread workflow, in an implementer session whose deployment claims `process` or `host` gets the text below through that seam's own typed error. Nothing announces the refusal in advance: the tool stays listed, because withdrawing it would tell the session what it is being kept away from.
84	
85	##### Start refusal
86	
87	```markdown
88	"<capability>" opens paths this process cannot confine and does not start in an implementer session under the "<claim>" isolation claim
89	```
90	
91	#### Token effect
92	
93	One short error in place of the child's result. A model that retries spends it again; the capability never starts, so no child tokens are spent at all.
94	
95	#### KV Cache effect
96	
97	Prefix-stable. No schema and no prompt section changes, so the refusal is an ordinary appended tool result.
98	
99	### Refused tool calls
100	
101	#### What the model sees
102	
103	An implementer session calling a tool whose definition declares an authority gets the tool registry's ordinary `Error: ` framing around the text below, and no recovery instruction, because no retry of the same call succeeds. `authority` is never model-visible on its own: `schemas()` whitelists name, description, and parameters, so the tool stays listed and callable-looking until it is called.
104	
105	##### Authority denial
106	
107	```markdown
108	"<tool>" carries the "<authority>" authority and is not callable in an implementer session
109	```
110	
111	#### Token effect
112	
113	One short error in place of the tool result, once per attempt. A model that retries the same tool spends that error again; nothing shortens the schema it keeps seeing.
114	
115	#### KV Cache effect
116	
117	Prefix-stable. The guard changes no schema and no prompt section, so the denial is an ordinary appended tool result.
118	
119	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
120	
121	- **A process runner denies whole directories, not reads** — `shell`, `subprocess`, and `terminal` deny through the sandbox backend's own mount, ruleset, or profile, so a confined process sees the denied directory as empty rather than receiving this package's message. Only `ctx.fs` reads carry the barrier's own refusal text.
122	- **`isolationClaim` is a deployment statement, not a grant** — raising it makes the out-of-process executors refuse and nothing else. A deployment that raises it without composing the enforcement still has its certificate refused, by the census rather than by this field.
123	- **The census is a snapshot** — it lists the tools the session started with. A tool registered afterwards is covered by the runtime guard and by the certificate rule that cross-checks each `request/header` against the census, not by the census itself.
124	- **The attestation proves an owner, not a run** — the barrier verifies that another operating-system account owns an unwritable file and records its digest; it does not yet compare that digest against the environment content hashes the `environment/run` stamp carries.
125	- **Trusted code in the implementer's own process** — a plugin with direct `Session` or `ctx.fs` access appends counterfeit refusals and reads any path. The barrier confines the composed executors, not the process.
126	- **Owner-only modes stop other accounts, not the model** — the `0700` root is protection against another operating-system user; the harness process runs as the same user as its tools, so the barrier, not the mode, is what denies the model.
127

1	# Cookbook: adding a workspace package
2	
3	English | [中文](adding-a-package.zh.md)
4	
5	The file-by-file checklist for a new `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>` package. This checklist is validated against the bash and adapter packages as templates; if it drifts from them, fix it here.
6	
7	## 1. Create the package
8	
9	```
10	packages/<group>/<pkg>/
11	  package.json     # copy from packages/core/tools, adjust name/description/deps
12	  tsconfig.json    # extends ../../../tsconfig.base.json, rootDir src,
13	                   # outDir lib/types, references: ../../../vendor/cosmokit,
14	                   # ../../../vendor/cordis (+ ../../../vendor/schemastery if
15	                   # you use Config, + ../../<group>/<dep> for each dsh dep)
16	  src/index.ts     # service default export or plugin (name/inject/apply/Config)
17	  README.md        # service API, events, extension points, design notes,
18	                   # + gated Model Experience context blocks or short form
19	                   # + the gated "Known Limitations and Deferred Work" section
20	                   # (or a whitelist entry in scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts)
21	```
22	
23	Choose an existing group when one matches the package's role (`core`, `llm`, `bash`, `compact`, `subagent`, `todo`, `session-persistence`, `ui`, `util`, or `support`). A new group is allowed, but it is a pure container: no `package.json`, no source files, and packages still sit exactly one level below it.
24	
25	package.json invariants (enforced by `pnpm run constraints` / `scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts`): `private: true`, a `version` matching the root `package.json`, `type: module`, `main: "lib/index.js"`, `types: "lib/types/index.d.ts"`, `exports["."].types: "./lib/types/index.d.ts"`, `exports["."].default: "./lib/index.js"`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis` in BOTH peerDependencies and devDependencies (same range). Mirror every dsh peer dependency in devDependencies. `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` goes in `dependencies` (it is a runtime validator), matching agent-loop. The `files` list contains exactly `lib/index.js`, `lib/invariant.js`, `lib/types/**/*.d.ts`, and package-specific runtime artifacts recognized by the gate; a package whose runtime export points into the emitted tree also includes `lib/types/**/*.js`. Do not publish `src`, declaration maps, JS maps, or stale root declaration files. CLI app packages with a package `bin` include `lib/bin.js` immediately after `lib/index.js` in `files`.
26	
27	In-package relative imports use explicit `.ts` specifiers in source (for example, `export * from './types.ts'`). The compiler rewrites those to `.js` in emitted JS and leaves explicit `.ts` specifiers in declarations, which standard NodeNext/Node16 TypeScript consumers resolve to the sibling `.d.ts` files.
28	
29	## 2. Register it in the root configs
30	
31	| File | Change |
32	|---|---|
33	| `tsconfig.base.json` | no edit for an existing group; for a new group, add a `./packages/<group>/*/src` candidate to the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` wildcard |
34	| `tsconfig.host.json` (Host package) or `tsconfig.client.json` (Client package) | add `{ "path": "./packages/<group>/<pkg>" }` to `references` — an ordinary package belongs to exactly one aggregate, never both. `api/remotes` uses a repository-specific split because the Host generates a contract that the Client consumes in a later phase; new packages must not copy it ([layout](../development.md#typescript-project-layout)) |
35	| `knip.json` | only if the package has entrypoints that repository discovery does not already cover |
36	
37	A `packages/client/*` package additionally extends `tsconfig.base.client.json` instead of `tsconfig.base.json`, and a client plugin package declares `dsh.client` in package.json, exports `./client`, and calls the shared tsdown preset (`packages/client/tsdown.client.ts`) — see [packages/client/AGENTS.md](../../packages/client/AGENTS.md) for the client-side contract.
38	
39	Covered automatically by globs or package-manifest discovery — no edits needed: root `package.json` workspaces, `scripts/publint-all.ts`, `tsdown.config.ts`, `.oxlintrc.json`, `scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts`.
40	
41	## 3. Decide the package topology
42	
43	For a swappable capability, separate Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles into packages when they evolve independently (see docs/architecture.md § "Capability seams" — the shell trio is the template). A single-purpose plugin stays one package.
44	
45	### Name the role that exists
46	
47	Name the stable current responsibility. Do not name the first implementation, a possible future expansion, or the Cordis base class. An interface package names the capability. An implementation package adds the mechanism, protocol, environment, or vendor that distinguishes it. Use `local` only when same-host execution is part of the contract.
48	
49	Use a singular `ctx` key for one engine, runtime, policy, controller, resolver, store, or current configuration. Use a plural key for a registry or a service that owns multiple named members. The class role and key number must agree. Do not reuse one Cordis `Context` key for incompatible host and client declarations. TypeScript declaration merging sees both faces even when they use separate runtime contexts. Add the role suffix when the natural plural already belongs to another face.
50	
51	| Word | Use it when | Do not use it when |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| `Controller` | It accepts commands or user intent and changes one existing domain or presentation state. | It executes arbitrary work, owns a provider fleet, or only converts values for display. |
54	| `Store` | It owns one data set and mainly offers CRUD, snapshot, or subscription operations for that data. | It validates a state machine, arbitrates authority, dispatches work, or owns provider precedence. A map does not make a class a store. |
55	| `Directory` | It exposes entries and metadata for discovery or selection. | Producers register arbitrary implementations into it, or callers execute work through it. |
56	| `Presenter` | It is a pure conversion from domain values or tool arguments to render intent. | It performs I/O, subscribes, mutates state, or owns lifecycle. |
57	| `Registry` | It owns a dynamic set of named registrations, including lookup, duplicate or precedence rules, lifetime, and disposal. | Its main contract is dispatch, execution, cancellation, policy, or orchestration. |
58	| `Runtime` | It runs live work and owns dispatch, cancellation, provider coordination, or operation lifecycle across calls. | It only stores records, returns a catalog, resolves one value, or holds configuration. |
59	| `Resolver` | It computes or locates one answer from supplied inputs without owning that answer's lifecycle. | It owns a mutable collection or long-running execution. |
60	| `Binder` | It attaches one declared interface to a caller context or lifecycle and returns the bound value. | It owns the value as a collection, controls its domain state, or only converts data. |
61	| `Engine` | It implements a domain algorithm or stateful execution model. | It only selects a provider or forwards across a protocol boundary. |
62	| `Policy` | It decides what is allowed, selected, limited, or observed. | It performs the mechanism that the decision permits. |
63	| `Executor` | It runs one explicit request or resolved specification in one capability. | It owns a broad application lifecycle or provider catalog. |
64	| `Gateway` | It adapts a process, network, RPC, or API boundary. | It only registers same-process services or stores metadata. |
65	| `Provider` | It supplies one implementation of a capability definition. Add a mechanism or vendor qualifier when several can exist. | It is the capability definition, provider registry, or consumer runtime. |
66	| `Backend` | It implements replaceable lower-level persistence, transport, or execution behind a defined interface. | It is a user-facing service or one returned live-resource reference. |
67	| `Handle` | It refers to one live resource and controls or observes that resource. | It creates and manages the complete resource pool. |
68	| `Config` | It owns one resolved configuration value or one tightly bounded record and its update contract. | It stores a general collection, executes work, or exposes unrelated settings. |
69	| `Service` | It owns a cohesive domain service that no sharper role above states honestly. | The name exists only because the class extends Cordis `Service`. |
70	
71	Use `SDK` only for the JSON-RPC client/server protocol used by the supported Python and TypeScript SDKs. DeepSeek Harness itself is an agent harness, not an SDK project. Use the canonical product spelling `Typert`, never `TypeRT` or `typeRT`.
72	
73	## 4. Write the package README
74	
75	Keep package-specific service API, config, events, extension points, and design notes first. The limitations section records durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints owned by this package; ordinary cleanup stays in its source TODO or Agent Note. An indirect Model Experience sentence may name the consumer that surfaces this package's contribution, but it does not restate that consumer's implementation. End a package README with this canonical sequence:
76	
77	````markdown
78	## Model Experience
79	
80	### Request context and condition
81	
82	#### What the model sees
83	
84	The exact data-dependent fields, an anchored generated-catalog link, or an introduction to the verbatim literal below.
85	
86	##### Verbatim text for this field, when needed
87	
88	```markdown
89	Stable system-prompt prose of any length, or another long non-generated literal, copied exactly from source.
90	```
91	
92	#### Token effect
93	
94	Fixed, conditional, retained, replaced, capped, or zero-direct token effect.
95	
96	#### KV Cache effect
97	
98	Append-only, prefix-stable, replacing, or independent behavior, including the exact conditions that may invalidate reuse.
99	
100	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
101	
102	- **Consumer-visible gap** — exact missing operation or case, its consequence, and any maintainer constraint.
103	````
104	
105	Fill Model Experience from the implementation. Use one H3 per direct, conditional, capped, lifetime, or auxiliary model-context entry, with the three ordered H4 fields shown above and one prose paragraph under each. Quote stable text owned by the package: system-prompt prose goes in a titled H5 plus `markdown` fence under the field that introduces it—normally `What the model sees`—other short literals stay inline with named placeholders, and other long literals use the same nested form. Summarize only data-dependent or provider-owned text. A tool-schema entry links its anchored section in the generated [tool catalog](../tool-catalog.md) and states only deltas absent there. Keep prompt and schema entries separate when scoping can hide one without the other. In `KV Cache effect`, distinguish append-only growth, a stable repeated prefix, replacement of earlier request tokens, and an independent model request, then name the package-owned changes that can invalidate reuse. “Does not invalidate” means the package preserves an already-reusable prefix; provider cache availability and eviction remain outside the package contract. The [prose standard](../../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) governs completeness and ownership; the verifier enforces the required section structure.
106	
107	A package with no context effect or one consumer-owned path uses the audited `None, as ` or `Indirectly, through ` sentence in [`SENTENCE_MODEL_EXPERIENCE`](../../scripts/verify-package-readme-model-experience.ts), followed by a `KV Cache effect` H4 and one non-empty paragraph; a model-agnostic generic package may instead join `NO_MODEL_EXPERIENCE_SECTION`. Do not expand either case into a description of another package's work. The limitations [allowlist](../../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) is independent. The [Model Experience Agent Note](../../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-12-package-model-experience-contract.md) records the rationale.
108	
109	## 5. Verify
110	
111	```sh
112	pnpm install        # registers the workspace
113	pnpm run doc-sync
114	pnpm run constraints && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run lint
115	pnpm run build && pnpm run hygiene
116	```
117	
118	Follow the [repository testing policy](../testing.md) for the behavior-specific checks and coverage required by the new package.
119

1	# AGENTS.md — The documentation standard
2	
3	This file defines document structure, Markdown tiers, writing rules, and `verify-doc-budgets` ceilings. Use [dsh-doc-standards](../.agents/skills/dsh-doc-standards/SKILL.md) for placement and validation, and [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment; the [doc-tiers Agent Note](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-04-doc-tiers-and-budgets.md) owns rationale.
4	
5	## Document structure
6	
7	These rules apply to human-facing documentation; [Agent Notes](../.agents/notes/README.md) remain outside their scope. A [postmortem](postmortem/README.md) is an incident-scoped reference; chronology records evidence, not a teaching sequence. A document's subject and tree position fix its scope: describe its own subject at appropriate detail and direct children only by purpose, responsibility, and high-level behavior; link to the owning descendant for lower-level detail. Document type does not widen that scope. A reference may be exhaustive only about its own subject. Testing mechanisms, fixtures, and harnesses belong at the lowest owning level; higher documents link there.
8	
9	Classify every in-scope document as a tutorial or reference. Tutorials follow an ordered path to an outcome and introduce only what each step needs. References define a lookup scope and current behavior without a teaching sequence. Separate substantial tutorial and reference content; label a section when either part is small.
10	
11	Before writing a tutorial, privately classify the reader's starting knowledge and each concept as beginner, intermediate, or advanced. Establish prerequisites before dependent concepts, increase difficulty gradually, and move unnecessary advanced material to a later tutorial or reference.
12	
13	Author in this order: locate the document in the tree; set its permitted detail; choose tutorial or reference; for a tutorial, order concepts by prerequisite and difficulty; relocate descendant-owned detail; replace lower-level explanations with links to their owners.
14	
15	## The tier taxonomy: one home per fact
16	
17	Each fact has one home: the tier whose job it is; elsewhere, link there.
18	
19	| Tier | Job | Does NOT belong there |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| Root `AGENTS.md` | Standing orders: rules an agent needs in context in every session, one to three lines each, linking its home | Stories, worked examples, situational procedures, anything restated from a linked home |
22	| Subtree `AGENTS.md` (`packages/`, `examples/`, `docs/`, `.agents/notes/`) | Orders specific to that subtree | Repo-wide rules the root file already carries |
23	| [architecture.md](architecture.md) | Ordered map: composition, core packages, loop, seams, extension points; read before changing `packages/` | Type definitions (→ subsystems), per-package detail (→ package READMEs), decision rationale (→ Agent Notes), implementation-status annotations |
24	| [subsystems/](subsystems/README.md) | One reference page per subsystem: type definitions, semantics, and the generated Cordis API | Behavior narration (→ architecture.md) |
25	| [Agent Notes](../.agents/notes/README.md) | Active decision records: the why, what-was-given-up, and required verification; `implemented/` notes describe shipped reality in present tense | Migration plans, acceptance-task checklists, fixture walkthroughs, and spec-speak ("should…") once the decision has shipped; archived notes are frozen history, never current authority |
26	| [postmortem/](postmortem/README.md) | Incident stories — the only tier where war-story narrative belongs | — |
27	| [cookbook/](cookbook/adding-a-package.md) | Step-by-step how-tos with numbered verify steps | Design rationale (→ the Agent Note each guide links) |
28	| [user/](user/index.md) | Product-facing guides published by the documentation website | Generated reference tables, contributor procedures, decision history |
29	| Package README | The per-package contract: config, semantics, limitations, extension points, and [Model Experience](cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme) | JSDoc restatement, generated-catalog restatement (event/tool tables), other packages' concerns |
30	| [development.md](development.md) | Contributor setup, daily workflow, and a summary of CI; a bilingual pair under the [i18n contract](i18n/README.md) | Runtime/version rationale (→ Agent Notes), check-by-check lists that drift from `package.json` scripts |
31	| Generated reference: the per-page `cordis-surface` regions in [subsystems/](subsystems/README.md), the [Cordis core API + inherited tier](cordis-api/context.md), [tool-catalog](tool-catalog.md), [config-catalog](config-catalog.md), [persistence-catalog](persistence-catalog.md), [module-graph.md](module-graph.md) | Exhaustive English sources regenerated from source and freshness-gated; reviewed Chinese counterparts follow the [pairing workflow](i18n/README.md#scope-and-exclusions) | Hand edits to generated English sources or regions; Chinese counterparts update through pairing only |
32	| Skills (`.agents/skills/`) | Reusable workflows and specialized decision standards | Product and runtime contracts (→ docs or source) |
33	
34	Placement: bugs → postmortems; rationale → Agent Notes; procedures → cookbooks; type definitions → subsystems; package contracts → READMEs; standing orders → root `AGENTS.md` with a rationale link.
35	
36	## Writing rules
37	
38	- **Document current state, not change history.** Avoid "previously/now/no longer", PRs, commits, and stack positions in durable prose; name the live mechanism. Put change stories in commits, PRs, Agent Notes, or postmortems; the latter two may cite merged PRs and issues as evidence.
39	- **Every non-trivial change includes at least one Agent Note in the same PR.** Update the owning note or add one; only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](../.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)).
40	- **One physical line per paragraph** (`verify-md-wrap`): use editor soft-wrap. Code blocks, tables, and list structure keep their formatting; code comments stay under the linter's column limit.
41	- **Fenced `ts` blocks must compile** (`doc-typecheck`); a pasted type declaration and its original JSDoc use ` ```ts type-equiv `, while a body-stripped public class declaration uses ` ```ts public-api `; register either in the manifest so neither can drift ([mechanics](development.md#documenting-types-verbatim-ts-type-equiv)).
42	- **The owning [subsystems page](subsystems/README.md) updates in the same change** that reshapes a documented type. `verify-type-equiv` catches drifted pastes, not never-documented new types; a type is documented on its declaring package group's page ([page scoping](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-03-package-anchored-subsystem-pages.md)).
43	- **Pairs update together**: [Terminology-guided](i18n/terminology.md), single-pass active-agent work repositions first-use annotations, preserves untouched prose, and re-records; `dsh-translate-docs` remains user-invoked ([contract](i18n/README.md)).
44	- **Comments and JSDoc state complete contracts, not reasoning transcripts.** Preserve behavior, failure, timing, ownership, modality, exceptions, consequences, and non-obvious orientation; delete narration, test walkthroughs, review analysis, and code restatement. Keep the local contract and link its rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for details.
45	- Write directly: name actors and facts ([decision](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-09-concrete-prose-names-actors-and-recorded-facts.md)). Reserve `seam` for the defined capability. Name the exact check, type, API, operation, or behavior instead of metaphorical "gate", "vocabulary", or "surface".
46	
47	## Wordcount Budgets
48	
49	[scripts/doc-budgets.manifest.json](../scripts/doc-budgets.manifest.json) sets standing-doc ceilings; `pnpm run verify-doc-budgets` rejects excess or missing files.
50	
51	When the gate goes red:
52	
53	1. **Relocate** content that belongs in another tier; leave a one-line link if needed.
54	2. **Condense** content that belongs here but can be shorter.
55	3. **Raise** the ceiling only when the words need the space; justify the manifest diff in the PR. A too-low ceiling is a budget bug.
56	
57	Ceilings are guardrails, not reduction targets. At or below target, retain at least 5% headroom; above target, freeze the ceiling until relocation or condensation brings the document under target. Lower a ceiling only when the document still has room, and raise it when content would otherwise be deleted. Targets: root `AGENTS.md` ≤ 1,600 words; `architecture.md` ≤ 1,800; subtree `AGENTS.md` ≤ 600, except `packages/AGENTS.md` ≤ 650 and this file ≤ 1,250; `packages/README.md` ≤ 600. Review governs unbudgeted tiers.
58	
59	## The slop checklist
60	
61	Hunt these in any doc; [dsh-doc-standards](../.agents/skills/dsh-doc-standards/SKILL.md) runs this list as an audit:
62	
63	- The same rule stated in more than one home. Grep a distinctive phrase; keep one home and link the rest.
64	- Narrated history or war stories: "previously", "now", "no longer", "used to", "renamed", "was moved", PRs, or commits. State the current fact; link an Agent Note or postmortem when needed.
65	- Implementation-status annotations in prose or diagrams ("implemented!", "future: …"). Status rots; the repo layout and package manifests carry it.
66	- Hand-restated catalogs, JSDoc, or inventories of tests, packages, and status when source or a generator is authoritative.
67	- Reasoning transcripts: step-by-step implementation narration, proof of obvious branches, test walkthroughs, or rejected local alternatives. Keep the resulting contract or durable rationale; delete the path used to derive it.
68	- Rationale repeated beside sibling methods instead of once at the owning capability or helper.
69	- Paragraph walls: one paragraph carrying several rules and parenthetical asides. Split it or demote the detail to its home.
70	- Emphasis inflation: bold, CAPS, or "critically" everywhere means nothing stands out. Reserve emphasis for the clause that changes behavior.
71	- Spec-speak in `implemented/` Agent Notes: "should", migration plans, acceptance checklists. An implemented Agent Note describes what is, per the [implemented-note instructions](../.agents/notes/implemented/AGENTS.md).
72	
73	## Cross-reference with machine-checkable links, never free prose
74	
75	Link repository references with relative Markdown paths, never bare filenames or Agent Note numbers. `verify-md-links` rejects missing targets and dead `#fragment` anchors ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-06-18-markdown-cross-link-lint.md)).
76

22	  mountRefusal?: string

33	describe('tool authority and the enforcement-backed certificate through a real cordis.yml', () => {
34	  it('refuses the composition, denies the late tool, and certifies only what the census proves', async () => {
35	    const { stdout, stderr } = await runLoaderSmoke({
36	      label: 'read-barrier-guard',
37	      tempDirPrefix: 'read-barrier-guard-e2e-',
38	      binScript,
39	      libBinScript: binScript,
40	      configPath,
41	      binArgs: [configPath],
42	      tsconfigPath: repoTsconfig,
43	      env: { DSH_READ_BARRIER_GUARD_PRESETS: presetsRoot },
44	    })
45	    expect(stderr).toBe('')
46	    const result = JSON.parse(stdout.trimEnd().split('\n').at(-1) ?? '') as DriverResult
47	    expect(result.type).toBe('result')
48	
49	    // The mount audit refuses an implementer composition that holds a
50	    // log-reading tool, naming the tool and the authority to remove.
51	    expect(result.mountRefusal).toBe(
52	      'agent-presets: preset "log-reading" declares role "implementer" but composes "session_search", which carries the "session-log" authority',
53	    )
54	    expect(result.refusedSessionExists).toBe(false)
55	    // The same tools compose freely for a preset that claims no role.
56	    expect(result.openTools).toContain('session_search')
57	    expect(result.implementerTools).not.toContain('session_search')
58	
59	    // The guard covers what no composition audit saw: a tool registered into
60	    // the agent's own layer afterwards. It is visible and still not callable.
61	    expect(result.implementerTools).toContain('late_session_read')
62	    expect(result.guarded).toEqual({
63	      isError: true,
64	      text: 'Error: "late_session_read" carries the "session-log" authority and is not callable in an implementer session',
65	    })
66	
67	    // The census is the durable answer to what the session composed.
68	    expect(result.scope).toMatchObject({
69	      version: 1,
70	      role: 'implementer',
71	      presetId: 'implementing',
72	      enforcement: [
73	        { capability: 'fs', state: 'denied-at-executor' },
74	        { capability: 'shell', state: 'not-composed' },
75	        { capability: 'subprocess', state: 'not-composed' },
76	        { capability: 'terminal', state: 'not-composed' },
77	        { capability: 'subagent', state: 'not-composed' },
78	        { capability: 'workflow', state: 'not-composed' },

80	    })
81	    // Every tool the session started with, and no authority among them.
82	    expect(result.scope?.census.map(entry => entry.name)).toContain('read')
83	    expect(result.scope?.census.every(entry => entry.authority.length === 0)).toBe(true)
84	    // The census is a snapshot: the tool registered after it is exactly what
85	    // the runtime guard, not the census, has to cover.
86	    expect(result.scope?.census.map(entry => entry.name)).not.toContain('late_session_read')
87	
88	    // `host` needs evidence from outside this process, which no in-process
89	    // component can produce for itself.
90	    expect(result.hostClaim).toEqual({
91	      certified: false,
92	      code: 'VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN',
93	      message: 'run cannot claim "host" isolation: no verified read-barrier/attestation places the standard outside this account',

95	    // An agent-reported run is the session's own account of its checks.

97	      certified: false,
98	      code: 'VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN',
99	      message: 'run cannot claim "process" isolation: the run was agent-reported, so no validator executed its checks',
100	    })
101	    // What the census does prove certifies, and carries the executor forward.
102	    expect(result.processClaim).toEqual({ certified: true, isolation: 'process', executor: 'runner' })
